  1 | # Efficiency Analyzer Service
  2 | 
  3 | A microservice that analyzes code complexity and recommends algorithmic optimizations. Part of the Algorithmic Debugging & Efficiency Coach system.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Features
  6 | 
  7 | - **Time Complexity Analysis**: Calculates Big O time complexity by analyzing loops, recursion, and function calls
  8 | - **Space Complexity Analysis**: Analyzes memory usage from data structures and call stacks
  9 | - **Pattern Detection**: Identifies common inefficient patterns:
 10 |   - Nested loops (O(n²), O(n³))
 11 |   - Redundant recursion without memoization
 12 |   - Linear search in loops
 13 |   - String concatenation in loops
 14 |   - Inefficient list operations
 15 |   - Repeated sorting
 16 | - **Optimization Recommendations**: Provides specific strategies:
 17 |   - Hash Map/Set for O(1) lookups
 18 |   - Dynamic Programming for recursion
 19 |   - Two Pointers for sorted arrays
 20 |   - Sliding Window for subarrays
 21 |   - Deque for efficient queue operations
 22 | - **Performance Estimation**: Estimates speedup for different input sizes
 23 | 
 24 | ## Architecture
 25 | 
 26 | - **Port**: 8002
 27 | - **Framework**: FastAPI
 28 | - **Language Support**: Python (primary), C++, Java (basic)
 29 | - **Analysis Engine**: AST-based code parsing and pattern matching
 30 | 
 31 | ## API Endpoints
 32 | 
 33 | ### Health Check
 34 | ```
 35 | GET /health
 36 | ```
 37 | 
 38 | **Response:**
 39 | ```json
 40 | {
 41 |   "status": "healthy",
 42 |   "service": "efficiency-analyzer",
 43 |   "version": "1.0.0"
 44 | }
 45 | ```
 46 | 
 47 | ### Analyze Code
 48 | ```
 49 | POST /api/v1/analyze
 50 | ```
 51 | 
 52 | **Request Body:**
 53 | ```json
 54 | {
 55 |   "language": "python",
 56 |   "code": "def find_duplicates(arr):\n    duplicates = []\n    for i in range(len(arr)):\n        for j in range(i+1, len(arr)):\n            if arr[i] == arr[j]:\n                duplicates.append(arr[i])\n    return duplicates",
 57 |   "context": "Array size can be up to 10000 elements"
 58 | }
 59 | ```
 60 | 
 61 | **Response:**
 62 | ```json
 63 | {
 64 |   "current_time_complexity": {
 65 |     "notation": "O(n²)",
 66 |     "explanation": "Quadratic time - nested iterations over the data. Contributing factors: Nested loops (2 levels): O(n²), Loop iterates n times, Loop with range iteration",
 67 |     "factors": [
 68 |       "Nested loops (2 levels): O(n²)",
 69 |       "Loop iterates n times",
 70 |       "Loop with range iteration"
 71 |     ]
 72 |   },
 73 |   "current_space_complexity": {
 74 |     "notation": "O(n)",
 75 |     "explanation": "Linear space - memory usage grows with input size. Contributing factors: List data structure(s): O(n) space",
 76 |     "factors": [
 77 |       "List data structure(s): O(n) space"
 78 |     ]
 79 |   },
 80 |   "target_time_complexity": "O(n)",
 81 |   "target_space_complexity": "O(1)",
 82 |   "inefficient_patterns": [
 83 |     {
 84 |       "pattern_type": "nested_loops",
 85 |       "severity": "medium",
 86 |       "line_numbers": [3, 4],
 87 |       "description": "Nested loops with 2 levels of nesting",
 88 |       "impact": "O(n^2) time complexity - performance degrades exponentially"
 89 |     }
 90 |   ],
 91 |   "optimization_strategies": [
 92 |     {
 93 |       "technique": "Hash Map / Set",
 94 |       "description": "Replace nested loops with hash-based lookups for O(1) access time",
 95 |       "steps": [
 96 |         "Identify the inner loop operation (usually a search or comparison)",
 97 |         "Create a hash map or set to store elements for O(1) lookup",
 98 |         "Replace inner loop with hash map lookup",
 99 |         "Reduce time complexity from O(n²) to O(n)"
100 |       ],
101 |       "complexity_improvement": "O(n²) → O(n)",
102 |       "code_example": "# Before: O(n²)\nfor i in range(len(arr)):\n    for j in range(len(arr)):\n        if arr[i] == arr[j]:\n            # ...\n\n# After: O(n)\nseen = set()\nfor item in arr:\n    if item in seen:\n        # ...\n    seen.add(item)"
103 |     }
104 |   ],
105 |   "estimated_improvement": {
106 |     "n=100": "10x faster",
107 |     "n=1000": "100x faster",
108 |     "n=10000": "1000x faster"
109 |   },
110 |   "overall_score": 30
111 | }
112 | ```
113 | 
114 | ## Setup Instructions
115 | 
116 | ### Local Development
117 | 
118 | 1. **Install Dependencies**
119 |    ```bash
120 |    cd services/efficiency-analyzer
121 |    pip install -r requirements.txt
122 |    ```
123 | 
124 | 2. **Run the Service**
125 |    ```bash
126 |    python -m app.main
127 |    # Or using uvicorn directly
128 |    uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002 --reload
129 |    ```
130 | 
131 | 3. **Test the Service**
132 |    ```bash
133 |    curl http://localhost:8002/health
134 |    ```
135 | 
136 | ### Docker Deployment
137 | 
138 | 1. **Build Image**
139 |    ```bash
140 |    docker build -t efficiency-analyzer:latest .
141 |    ```
142 | 
143 | 2. **Run Container**
144 |    ```bash
145 |    docker run -p 8002:8002 efficiency-analyzer:latest
146 |    ```
147 | 
148 | ## Example Usage
149 | 
150 | ### Python Example: Nested Loops
151 | 
152 | **Input Code:**
153 | ```python
154 | def find_pairs(arr, target):
155 |     pairs = []
156 |     for i in range(len(arr)):
157 |         for j in range(i+1, len(arr)):
158 |             if arr[i] + arr[j] == target:
159 |                 pairs.append((arr[i], arr[j]))
160 |     return pairs
161 | ```
162 | 
163 | **Analysis Result:**
164 | - **Current Complexity**: O(n²) time, O(n) space
165 | - **Target Complexity**: O(n) time, O(n) space
166 | - **Pattern Detected**: Nested loops
167 | - **Recommendation**: Use hash map to store complements
168 | - **Estimated Improvement**: 100x faster for n=1000
169 | 
170 | **Optimized Code:**
171 | ```python
172 | def find_pairs(arr, target):
173 |     seen = set()
174 |     pairs = []
175 |     for num in arr:
176 |         complement = target - num
177 |         if complement in seen:
178 |             pairs.append((complement, num))
179 |         seen.add(num)
180 |     return pairs
181 | ```
182 | 
183 | ### Python Example: Redundant Recursion
184 | 
185 | **Input Code:**
186 | ```python
187 | def fibonacci(n):
188 |     if n <= 1:
189 |         return n
190 |     return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)
191 | ```
192 | 
193 | **Analysis Result:**
194 | - **Current Complexity**: O(2^n) time, O(n) space
195 | - **Target Complexity**: O(n) time, O(n) space
196 | - **Pattern Detected**: Binary recursion without memoization
197 | - **Recommendation**: Add memoization using @lru_cache
198 | - **Estimated Improvement**: Exponential to linear
199 | 
200 | **Optimized Code:**
201 | ```python
202 | from functools import lru_cache
203 | 
204 | @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
205 | def fibonacci(n):
206 |     if n <= 1:
207 |         return n
208 |     return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)
209 | ```
210 | 
211 | ## Complexity Analysis Details
212 | 
213 | ### Time Complexity Detection
214 | 
215 | The service analyzes:
216 | - **Loop Nesting**: Counts nested loop levels
217 | - **Recursion**: Identifies recursive calls and branching factor
218 | - **Built-in Operations**: Tracks complexity of sort(), in, etc.
219 | - **Data Structure Operations**: Analyzes list/dict/set operations
220 | 
221 | ### Space Complexity Detection
222 | 
223 | The service analyzes:
224 | - **Data Structures**: Lists, dicts, sets created
225 | - **Recursion Stack**: Call stack depth
226 | - **Auxiliary Space**: Temporary variables and collections
227 | 
228 | ### Pattern Detection
229 | 
230 | Common patterns identified:
231 | 1. **Nested Loops**: O(n²) or worse
232 | 2. **Redundant Recursion**: O(2^n) without memoization
233 | 3. **Linear Search in Loop**: O(n²) from nested searches
234 | 4. **String Concatenation**: O(n²) from immutability
235 | 5. **Inefficient List Ops**: O(n) operations in loops
236 | 6. **Repeated Sorting**: Multiple O(n log n) operations
237 | 
238 | ## Optimization Strategies
239 | 
240 | The service recommends:
241 | - **Hash-based Lookups**: O(1) instead of O(n)
242 | - **Dynamic Programming**: Memoization for recursion
243 | - **Two Pointers**: For sorted array problems
244 | - **Sliding Window**: For subarray problems
245 | - **Deque**: For efficient queue operations
246 | - **Binary Search**: For sorted data
247 | - **Sort Once**: Avoid repeated sorting
248 | 
249 | ## Limitations
250 | 
251 | - **Language Support**: Full analysis only for Python; basic for C++/Java
252 | - **Complex Algorithms**: May not detect all optimization opportunities
253 | - **Context-Dependent**: Some optimizations depend on use case
254 | - **Heuristic-Based**: Uses pattern matching, not formal verification
255 | 
256 | ## Integration
257 | 
258 | This service integrates with:
259 | - **Debugging Engine** (port 8001): Provides execution flow analysis
260 | - **watsonx Integration** (port 8003): AI-powered explanations
261 | - **Frontend** (port 3000): User interface
262 | 
263 | ## Development
264 | 
265 | ### Project Structure
266 | ```
267 | services/efficiency-analyzer/
268 | ├── app/
269 | │   ├── __init__.py
270 | │   ├── main.py                    # FastAPI application
271 | │   ├── models/                    # Request/response models
272 | │   ├── services/                  # Business logic
273 | │   ├── analyzers/                 # Complexity analyzers
274 | │   └── utils/                     # Utilities
275 | ├── requirements.txt
276 | ├── Dockerfile
277 | └── README.md
278 | ```
279 | 
280 | ### Adding New Patterns
281 | 
282 | To add a new inefficient pattern:
283 | 
284 | 1. Add detection logic in `app/analyzers/patterns.py`
285 | 2. Add optimization strategy in `app/services/optimizer.py`
286 | 3. Update pattern types in response models
287 | 
288 | ### Testing
289 | 
290 | ```bash
291 | # Run with test code
292 | curl -X POST http://localhost:8002/api/v1/analyze \
293 |   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
294 |   -d '{
295 |     "language": "python",
296 |     "code": "def test():\n    for i in range(n):\n        for j in range(n):\n            print(i, j)"
297 |   }'
298 | ```
299 | 
300 | ## License
301 | 
302 | Part of the IBM BOB Hackathon project.
</content>

<content lines="1-439">
  1 | # watsonx.ai Integration Service
  2 | 
  3 | AI-powered code generation, refactoring, and explanation service using IBM watsonx.ai.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Overview
  6 | 
  7 | This service integrates with IBM watsonx.ai to provide intelligent code operations:
  8 | - **Code Generation**: Generate optimized code from natural language descriptions
  9 | - **Code Refactoring**: Optimize existing code while preserving functionality
 10 | - **Code Explanation**: Generate educational explanations of code with analogies
 11 | 
 12 | ## Architecture
 13 | 
 14 | The service is built as a serverless function using FastAPI and integrates with:
 15 | - **IBM watsonx.ai**: Primary AI engine using granite-20b-code-instruct model
 16 | - **Debugging Engine** (port 8001): Provides bug reports for context
 17 | - **Efficiency Analyzer** (port 8002): Provides complexity analysis for context
 18 | 
 19 | ### Key Components
 20 | 
 21 | ```
 22 | watsonx-ai-integration/
 23 | ├── app/
 24 | │   ├── handler.py              # FastAPI application & endpoints
 25 | │   ├── models/                 # Request/response models
 26 | │   ├── services/               # Core services
 27 | │   │   ├── watsonx_client.py   # watsonx.ai API client (with mock mode)
 28 | │   │   ├── code_generator.py   # Code generation service
 29 | │   │   ├── refactoring.py      # Code refactoring service
 30 | │   │   └── explainer.py        # Code explanation service
 31 | │   ├── prompts/                # Prompt templates
 32 | │   └── utils/                  # Utilities
 33 | ```
 34 | 
 35 | ## watsonx.ai Integration Details
 36 | 
 37 | ### Models Used
 38 | 
 39 | - **Primary Model**: `ibm/granite-20b-code-instruct`
 40 |   - Used for: Complex code generation, refactoring
 41 |   - Temperature: 0.2-0.7 depending on task
 42 |   - Max tokens: 2048
 43 | 
 44 | - **Fast Model**: `ibm/granite-8b-code-base`
 45 |   - Used for: Simple explanations, quick tasks
 46 |   - Temperature: 0.4-0.8
 47 |   - Max tokens: 1024
 48 | 
 49 | ### Prompt Engineering
 50 | 
 51 | The service uses structured prompts with:
 52 | - Few-shot examples for better results
 53 | - Explicit formatting instructions (JSON output)
 54 | - Context from debugging and efficiency analysis
 55 | - Audience-level adaptation (beginner/intermediate/advanced)
 56 | 
 57 | ## API Documentation
 58 | 
 59 | ### Base URL
 60 | ```
 61 | http://localhost:8003
 62 | ```
 63 | 
 64 | ### Endpoints
 65 | 
 66 | #### 1. Health Check
 67 | ```http
 68 | GET /health
 69 | ```
 70 | 
 71 | **Response:**
 72 | ```json
 73 | {
 74 |   "status": "healthy",
 75 |   "service": "watsonx-ai-integration",
 76 |   "version": "1.0.0",
 77 |   "watsonx_connected": true,
 78 |   "mock_mode": true
 79 | }
 80 | ```
 81 | 
 82 | #### 2. Generate Code
 83 | ```http
 84 | POST /generate
 85 | ```
 86 | 
 87 | **Request Body:**
 88 | ```json
 89 | {
 90 |   "problem_description": "Find all pairs in an array that sum to a target value",
 91 |   "language": "python",
 92 |   "constraints": "Must be O(n) time complexity",
 93 |   "optimization_target": "time_complexity",
 94 |   "include_comments": true,
 95 |   "examples": [
 96 |     {
 97 |       "input": "[2, 7, 11, 15], target=9",
 98 |       "output": "[(0, 1)]"
 99 |     }
100 |   ]
101 | }
102 | ```
103 | 
104 | **Response:**
105 | ```json
106 | {
107 |   "job_id": "gen_abc123",
108 |   "status": "completed",
109 |   "operation_type": "generate",
110 |   "generated_code": {
111 |     "code": "def two_sum(nums, target):\n    seen = {}\n    for i, num in enumerate(nums):\n        complement = target - num\n        if complement in seen:\n            return [seen[complement], i]\n        seen[num] = i\n    return []",
112 |     "language": "python",
113 |     "algorithm_used": "Hash Map",
114 |     "complexity_analysis": {
115 |       "time": "O(n)",
116 |       "space": "O(n)"
117 |     },
118 |     "explanation": "Uses a hash map to store seen numbers...",
119 |     "test_cases": [...]
120 |   },
121 |   "confidence_score": 0.95,
122 |   "processing_time_ms": 1250.5,
123 |   "model_used": "ibm/granite-20b-code-instruct",
124 |   "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
125 |   "completed_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:01Z"
126 | }
127 | ```
128 | 
129 | #### 3. Refactor Code
130 | ```http
131 | POST /refactor
132 | ```
133 | 
134 | **Request Body:**
135 | ```json
136 | {
137 |   "original_code": "def find_duplicates(arr):\n    duplicates = []\n    for i in range(len(arr)):\n        for j in range(i+1, len(arr)):\n            if arr[i] == arr[j]:\n                duplicates.append(arr[i])\n    return duplicates",
138 |   "language": "python",
139 |   "inefficient_patterns": ["nested_loops", "O(n^2)_time"],
140 |   "target_complexity": "O(n) time",
141 |   "optimization_focus": "time_complexity",
142 |   "include_explanation": true
143 | }
144 | ```
145 | 
146 | **Response:**
147 | ```json
148 | {
149 |   "job_id": "ref_xyz789",
150 |   "status": "completed",
151 |   "operation_type": "refactor",
152 |   "refactored_code": {
153 |     "original_code": "...",
154 |     "refactored_code": "def find_duplicates(arr):\n    seen = set()\n    duplicates = set()\n    for num in arr:\n        if num in seen:\n            duplicates.add(num)\n        seen.add(num)\n    return list(duplicates)",
155 |     "changes_made": [
156 |       "Replaced nested loops with single pass",
157 |       "Used hash set for O(1) lookups"
158 |     ],
159 |     "complexity_improvement": {
160 |       "before": {"time": "O(n²)", "space": "O(k)"},
161 |       "after": {"time": "O(n)", "space": "O(n)"}
162 |     },
163 |     "diff": "...",
164 |     "explanation": "Replaced O(n²) nested loop approach..."
165 |   },
166 |   "confidence_score": 0.92,
167 |   "processing_time_ms": 1450.2,
168 |   "model_used": "ibm/granite-20b-code-instruct"
169 | }
170 | ```
171 | 
172 | #### 4. Explain Code
173 | ```http
174 | POST /explain
175 | ```
176 | 
177 | **Request Body:**
178 | ```json
179 | {
180 |   "code": "def factorial(n):\n    if n == 0:\n        return 1\n    return n * factorial(n-1)",
181 |   "language": "python",
182 |   "explanation_level": "beginner",
183 |   "focus_areas": ["algorithm", "recursion"],
184 |   "include_analogies": true,
185 |   "bug_report": {
186 |     "has_errors": false,
187 |     "logic_errors": [...]
188 |   },
189 |   "complexity_analysis": {
190 |     "time_complexity": "O(n)",
191 |     "space_complexity": "O(n)"
192 |   }
193 | }
194 | ```
195 | 
196 | **Response:**
197 | ```json
198 | {
199 |   "job_id": "exp_def456",
200 |   "status": "completed",
201 |   "operation_type": "explain",
202 |   "explanation": {
203 |     "summary": "This function calculates factorial using recursion...",
204 |     "detailed_explanation": "The function works by calling itself...",
205 |     "key_concepts": ["recursion", "base case", "call stack"],
206 |     "potential_issues": [
207 |       {
208 |         "type": "missing_validation",
209 |         "description": "No check for negative numbers"
210 |       }
211 |     ],
212 |     "suggestions": [
213 |       "Add input validation",
214 |       "Consider iterative approach for large values"
215 |     ],
216 |     "learning_resources": [...],
217 |     "analogies": [
218 |       "Think of recursion like Russian nesting dolls..."
219 |     ]
220 |   },
221 |   "confidence_score": 0.88,
222 |   "processing_time_ms": 980.3
223 | }
224 | ```
225 | 
226 | #### 5. Get Job Status
227 | ```http
228 | GET /jobs/{job_id}
229 | ```
230 | 
231 | #### 6. Cancel Job
232 | ```http
233 | DELETE /jobs/{job_id}
234 | ```
235 | 
236 | ## Setup Instructions
237 | 
238 | ### Prerequisites
239 | - Python 3.11+
240 | - Docker (optional)
241 | - IBM watsonx.ai API credentials (for production)
242 | 
243 | ### Environment Variables
244 | 
245 | Create a `.env` file:
246 | ```bash
247 | # watsonx.ai Configuration
248 | WATSONX_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
249 | WATSONX_PROJECT_ID=your_project_id_here
250 | WATSONX_API_URL=https://us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com
251 | 
252 | # Service Configuration
253 | PORT=8003
254 | MOCK_MODE=true  # Set to false for production
255 | 
256 | # Optional
257 | LOG_LEVEL=INFO
258 | ```
259 | 
260 | ### Local Development
261 | 
262 | 1. **Install dependencies:**
263 | ```bash
264 | cd services/watsonx-ai-integration
265 | pip install -r requirements.txt
266 | ```
267 | 
268 | 2. **Run the service:**
269 | ```bash
270 | python -m app.handler
271 | ```
272 | 
273 | 3. **Access the API:**
274 | - Service: http://localhost:8003
275 | - API Docs: http://localhost:8003/docs
276 | - Health: http://localhost:8003/health
277 | 
278 | ### Docker Deployment
279 | 
280 | 1. **Build the image:**
281 | ```bash
282 | docker build -t watsonx-ai-integration:latest .
283 | ```
284 | 
285 | 2. **Run the container:**
286 | ```bash
287 | docker run -p 8003:8003 \
288 |   -e WATSONX_API_KEY=your_key \
289 |   -e WATSONX_PROJECT_ID=your_project \
290 |   -e MOCK_MODE=false \
291 |   watsonx-ai-integration:latest
292 | ```
293 | 
294 | ## Mock Mode
295 | 
296 | The service includes a **mock mode** for development without watsonx.ai credentials:
297 | 
298 | - Simulates API latency (500-1500ms)
299 | - Returns plausible responses based on prompt analysis
300 | - Useful for testing integration and UI development
301 | - Enable with `MOCK_MODE=true` (default)
302 | 
303 | ### Mock Response Examples
304 | 
305 | **Code Generation:**
306 | - Detects "two sum" → Returns hash map solution
307 | - Generic problems → Returns template code
308 | 
309 | **Refactoring:**
310 | - Returns optimized version with hash set pattern
311 | - Includes complexity improvements
312 | 
313 | **Explanation:**
314 | - Returns structured explanation with concepts and suggestions
315 | 
316 | ## Performance Benchmarks
317 | 
318 | ### Mock Mode
319 | - Code Generation: ~500-1500ms
320 | - Refactoring: ~600-1200ms
321 | - Explanation: ~400-1000ms
322 | 
323 | ### Real API (Expected)
324 | - Code Generation: ~2000-4000ms
325 | - Refactoring: ~2500-4500ms
326 | - Explanation: ~1500-3000ms
327 | 
328 | ## Model Selection Guide
329 | 
330 | | Task | Complexity | Model | Temperature |
331 | |------|-----------|-------|-------------|
332 | | Simple explanation | Low | granite-8b | 0.6-0.8 |
333 | | Code generation | Medium | granite-20b | 0.5-0.7 |
334 | | Complex refactoring | High | granite-20b | 0.2-0.3 |
335 | | Beginner explanation | Low | granite-8b | 0.8 |
336 | | Advanced explanation | High | granite-20b | 0.4 |
337 | 
338 | ## Integration with Other Services
339 | 
340 | ### With Debugging Engine
341 | ```python
342 | # Get bug report from debugging engine
343 | bug_report = requests.post("http://localhost:8001/analyze", json={...}).json()
344 | 
345 | # Request explanation with bug context
346 | explanation = requests.post("http://localhost:8003/explain", json={
347 |     "code": code,
348 |     "language": "python",
349 |     "bug_report": bug_report,
350 |     "focus_areas": ["bugs"]
351 | }).json()
352 | ```
353 | 
354 | ### With Efficiency Analyzer
355 | ```python
356 | # Get complexity analysis
357 | analysis = requests.post("http://localhost:8002/analyze", json={...}).json()
358 | 
359 | # Request refactoring with analysis context
360 | refactored = requests.post("http://localhost:8003/refactor", json={
361 |     "original_code": code,
362 |     "language": "python",
363 |     "inefficient_patterns": analysis["inefficient_patterns"],
364 |     "target_complexity": "O(n)"
365 | }).json()
366 | ```
367 | 
368 | ## Testing
369 | 
370 | Run tests:
371 | ```bash
372 | pytest tests/ -v
373 | ```
374 | 
375 | Run with coverage:
376 | ```bash
377 | pytest tests/ --cov=app --cov-report=html
378 | ```
379 | 
380 | ## Limitations
381 | 
382 | ### Current Implementation
383 | - In-memory job storage (use Redis for production)
384 | - Synchronous processing (can be made async with webhooks)
385 | - Basic syntax validation only
386 | - Mock mode for development
387 | 
388 | ### Production Considerations
389 | - Implement persistent job storage (Redis/PostgreSQL)
390 | - Add rate limiting and authentication
391 | - Implement webhook callbacks for long-running jobs
392 | - Add comprehensive error handling and retries
393 | - Monitor API usage and costs
394 | - Implement caching for common requests
395 | 
396 | ## Troubleshooting
397 | 
398 | ### Common Issues
399 | 
400 | 1. **Service won't start:**
401 |    - Check port 8003 is available
402 |    - Verify Python version (3.11+)
403 |    - Check all dependencies installed
404 | 
405 | 2. **Mock mode not working:**
406 |    - Ensure `MOCK_MODE=true` in environment
407 |    - Check logs for initialization messages
408 | 
409 | 3. **Real API errors:**
410 |    - Verify watsonx.ai credentials
411 |    - Check API key permissions
412 |    - Ensure project ID is correct
413 |    - Check network connectivity
414 | 
415 | ## Contributing
416 | 
417 | When adding new features:
418 | 1. Update prompt templates in `app/prompts/`
419 | 2. Add corresponding service methods
420 | 3. Update API documentation
421 | 4. Add tests
422 | 5. Update this README
423 | 
424 | ## License
425 | 
426 | Made with Bob
427 | 
428 | ## Support
429 | 
430 | For issues or questions:
431 | - Check logs: Service logs to stdout
432 | - Review API docs: http://localhost:8003/docs
433 | - Check architecture: See `ARCHITECTURE.md`
434 | 
435 | ---
436 | 
437 | **Service Status:** ✅ Operational (Mock Mode)  
438 | **Port:** 8003  
439 | **Version:** 1.0.0

<content lines="1-295">
  1 | # watsonx Orchestrate Integration Service
  2 | 
  3 | Workflow automation service that integrates with IBM watsonx Orchestrate for documentation updates, ticket creation, and learning path generation.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Overview
  6 | 
  7 | This service automates post-analysis workflows by:
  8 | - **Documentation Updates**: Automatically updating code documentation with complexity analysis
  9 | - **Ticket Creation**: Creating refactoring tickets in Jira/GitHub based on analysis results
 10 | - **Learning Path Generation**: Generating personalized learning paths for developers based on skill gaps
 11 | 
 12 | ## Architecture
 13 | 
 14 | - **Port**: 8004
 15 | - **Framework**: FastAPI
 16 | - **Integration**: IBM watsonx Orchestrate
 17 | - **Mock Mode**: Enabled by default for development
 18 | 
 19 | ## Features
 20 | 
 21 | ### 1. Post-Analysis Workflow
 22 | Triggered after code analysis completes:
 23 | - Updates documentation with complexity findings
 24 | - Creates tickets for identified issues
 25 | - Sends notifications to stakeholders
 26 | 
 27 | ### 2. Optimization Workflow
 28 | Triggered when optimization is applied:
 29 | - Updates documentation with new complexity
 30 | - Closes related tickets
 31 | - Logs performance improvements
 32 | 
 33 | ### 3. Developer Growth Workflow
 34 | Triggered periodically or on-demand:
 35 | - Analyzes historical code submissions
 36 | - Identifies skill gaps
 37 | - Generates personalized learning paths
 38 | - Schedules follow-up assessments
 39 | 
 40 | ## API Endpoints
 41 | 
 42 | ### Health Check
 43 | ```bash
 44 | GET /health
 45 | ```
 46 | 
 47 | ### Trigger Workflow
 48 | ```bash
 49 | POST /workflow/trigger
 50 | Content-Type: application/json
 51 | 
 52 | {
 53 |   "workflow_type": "post_analysis",
 54 |   "analysis_results": {
 55 |     "file_path": "src/algorithms/sort.py",
 56 |     "complexity": {"time": "O(n^2)", "space": "O(1)"},
 57 |     "issues": ["nested loops", "inefficient sorting"]
 58 |   },
 59 |   "developer_id": "dev123",
 60 |   "project_id": "proj456"
 61 | }
 62 | ```
 63 | 
 64 | ### Get Workflow Status
 65 | ```bash
 66 | GET /workflow/status/{job_id}
 67 | ```
 68 | 
 69 | ### Webhook Handler
 70 | ```bash
 71 | POST /webhook
 72 | Content-Type: application/json
 73 | 
 74 | {
 75 |   "event_type": "ticket_created",
 76 |   "payload": {"ticket_id": "PROJ-123"},
 77 |   "source": "jira",
 78 |   "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
 79 | }
 80 | ```
 81 | 
 82 | ## Setup
 83 | 
 84 | ### Prerequisites
 85 | - Python 3.11+
 86 | - pip
 87 | 
 88 | ### Installation
 89 | 
 90 | 1. Install dependencies:
 91 | ```bash
 92 | pip install -r requirements.txt
 93 | ```
 94 | 
 95 | 2. Set environment variables (optional):
 96 | ```bash
 97 | export ORCHESTRATE_API_KEY="your-api-key"
 98 | export ORCHESTRATE_API_URL="https://api.orchestrate.ibm.com"
 99 | export ORCHESTRATE_MOCK_MODE="false"  # Set to false for production
100 | export TICKETING_SYSTEM="jira"  # or "github"
101 | export TICKETING_API_TOKEN="your-token"
102 | export TICKETING_PROJECT_KEY="PROJ"
103 | ```
104 | 
105 | 3. Run the service:
106 | ```bash
107 | python -m app.handler
108 | ```
109 | 
110 | The service will start on `http://localhost:8004`
111 | 
112 | ### Docker Deployment
113 | 
114 | ```bash
115 | docker build -t watsonx-orchestrate-integration .
116 | docker run -p 8004:8004 watsonx-orchestrate-integration
117 | ```
118 | 
119 | ## Configuration
120 | 
121 | ### Mock Mode
122 | By default, the service runs in mock mode for development:
123 | - Simulates watsonx Orchestrate API responses
124 | - Generates mock tickets and documentation
125 | - No actual API calls are made
126 | 
127 | To disable mock mode:
128 | ```bash
129 | export ORCHESTRATE_MOCK_MODE="false"
130 | export TICKETING_MOCK_MODE="false"
131 | export DOCS_MOCK_MODE="false"
132 | ```
133 | 
134 | ### Ticketing System Integration
135 | 
136 | #### Jira
137 | ```bash
138 | export TICKETING_SYSTEM="jira"
139 | export TICKETING_API_URL="https://your-domain.atlassian.net"
140 | export TICKETING_API_TOKEN="your-jira-token"
141 | export TICKETING_PROJECT_KEY="PROJ"
142 | ```
143 | 
144 | #### GitHub Issues
145 | ```bash
146 | export TICKETING_SYSTEM="github"
147 | export TICKETING_API_TOKEN="your-github-token"
148 | export TICKETING_PROJECT_KEY="owner/repo"
149 | ```
150 | 
151 | ## Usage Examples
152 | 
153 | ### Example 1: Post-Analysis Workflow
154 | 
155 | ```python
156 | import requests
157 | 
158 | response = requests.post("http://localhost:8004/workflow/trigger", json={
159 |     "workflow_type": "post_analysis",
160 |     "analysis_results": {
161 |         "file_path": "src/algorithms/sort.py",
162 |         "complexity": {
163 |             "time_complexity": "O(n^2)",
164 |             "space_complexity": "O(1)"
165 |         },
166 |         "issues": [
167 |             "Inefficient nested loops",
168 |             "Missing edge case handling"
169 |         ],
170 |         "suggestions": [
171 |             "Replace bubble sort with merge sort",
172 |             "Add input validation"
173 |         ]
174 |     },
175 |     "developer_id": "dev123",
176 |     "project_id": "proj456"
177 | })
178 | 
179 | job_id = response.json()["job_id"]
180 | print(f"Workflow started: {job_id}")
181 | ```
182 | 
183 | ### Example 2: Optimization Workflow
184 | 
185 | ```python
186 | response = requests.post("http://localhost:8004/workflow/trigger", json={
187 |     "workflow_type": "optimization",
188 |     "analysis_results": {
189 |         "file_path": "src/algorithms/sort.py",
190 |         "before_complexity": {"time": "O(n^2)", "space": "O(1)"},
191 |         "after_complexity": {"time": "O(n log n)", "space": "O(n)"},
192 |         "changes_made": ["Replaced bubble sort with merge sort"],
193 |         "performance_improvement": {"percentage": 75}
194 |     },
195 |     "developer_id": "dev123",
196 |     "project_id": "proj456"
197 | })
198 | ```
199 | 
200 | ### Example 3: Developer Growth Workflow
201 | 
202 | ```python
203 | response = requests.post("http://localhost:8004/workflow/trigger", json={
204 |     "workflow_type": "developer_growth",
205 |     "analysis_results": {
206 |         "submissions": [
207 |             {"file": "solution1.py", "issues": ["inefficient DP"]},
208 |             {"file": "solution2.py", "issues": ["poor graph traversal"]}
209 |         ],
210 |         "skill_level": "intermediate"
211 |     },
212 |     "developer_id": "dev123",
213 |     "project_id": "proj456"
214 | })
215 | ```
216 | 
217 | ## Testing
218 | 
219 | Run the test suite:
220 | ```bash
221 | python test_service.py
222 | ```
223 | 
224 | ## Project Structure
225 | 
226 | ```
227 | watsonx-orchestrate-integration/
228 | ├── app/
229 | │   ├── __init__.py
230 | │   ├── handler.py              # Main FastAPI application
231 | │   ├── models/
232 | │   │   ├── request.py          # Request models
233 | │   │   └── response.py         # Response models
234 | │   ├── services/
235 | │   │   ├── orchestrate_client.py  # watsonx Orchestrate client
236 | │   │   ├── documentation.py       # Documentation service
237 | │   │   ├── ticketing.py           # Ticketing service
238 | │   │   └── learning_path.py       # Learning path service
239 | │   ├── workflows/
240 | │   │   ├── post_analysis.py       # Post-analysis workflow
241 | │   │   ├── optimization.py        # Optimization workflow
242 | │   │   └── developer_growth.py    # Developer growth workflow
243 | │   └── utils/
244 | │       └── logger.py              # Logging configuration
245 | ├── requirements.txt
246 | ├── Dockerfile
247 | ├── test_service.py
248 | └── README.md
249 | ```
250 | 
251 | ## Integration with Other Services
252 | 
253 | This service integrates with:
254 | - **Debugging Engine** (port 8001): Receives analysis results
255 | - **Efficiency Analyzer** (port 8002): Receives complexity analysis
256 | - **watsonx.ai Integration** (port 8003): Triggers AI-powered content generation
257 | 
258 | ## Mock vs Production Mode
259 | 
260 | ### Mock Mode (Development)
261 | - No actual API credentials required
262 | - Simulates all external API calls
263 | - Generates realistic mock responses
264 | - Logs what would be sent to real APIs
265 | 
266 | ### Production Mode
267 | - Requires valid API credentials
268 | - Makes actual API calls to watsonx Orchestrate
269 | - Creates real tickets in Jira/GitHub
270 | - Updates actual documentation files
271 | 
272 | ## Troubleshooting
273 | 
274 | ### Service won't start
275 | - Check if port 8004 is available
276 | - Verify Python version (3.11+)
277 | - Ensure all dependencies are installed
278 | 
279 | ### Workflows fail
280 | - Check logs for detailed error messages
281 | - Verify API credentials if not in mock mode
282 | - Ensure analysis results have required fields
283 | 
284 | ### Tickets not created
285 | - Verify ticketing system configuration
286 | - Check API token permissions
287 | - Review mock mode settings
288 | 
289 | ## License
290 | 
291 | IBM Confidential
292 | 
293 | ## Support
294 | 
295 | For issues or questions, contact the development team.
</content>

<content lines="1-253">
  1 | # CLI Demo Application
  2 | 
  3 | Interactive command-line interface for demonstrating the Algorithmic Debugging & Efficiency Coach system.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Overview
  6 | 
  7 | This CLI application provides an easy-to-use interface for testing and demonstrating the capabilities of the system, including:
  8 | 
  9 | - Code debugging analysis
 10 | - Efficiency and complexity analysis
 11 | - Code refactoring with watsonx.ai
 12 | - Automated workflow actions with watsonx Orchestrate
 13 | 
 14 | ## Features
 15 | 
 16 | - **Interactive Menu System**: User-friendly navigation
 17 | - **Example Code Analysis**: Pre-loaded examples demonstrating various issues
 18 | - **Custom Code Analysis**: Analyze your own code
 19 | - **Service Health Monitoring**: Check status of all microservices
 20 | - **Colored Output**: Clear, formatted results with syntax highlighting
 21 | - **Multiple Language Support**: Python, C++, and Java
 22 | 
 23 | ## Prerequisites
 24 | 
 25 | - Python 3.8 or higher
 26 | - All microservices running:
 27 |   - Debugging Engine (port 8001)
 28 |   - Efficiency Analyzer (port 8002)
 29 |   - watsonx.ai Integration (port 8003)
 30 |   - watsonx Orchestrate Integration (port 8004)
 31 | 
 32 | ## Installation
 33 | 
 34 | 1. Navigate to the CLI demo directory:
 35 | ```bash
 36 | cd demo/cli-demo
 37 | ```
 38 | 
 39 | 2. Install dependencies:
 40 | ```bash
 41 | pip install -r requirements.txt
 42 | ```
 43 | 
 44 | ## Usage
 45 | 
 46 | ### Starting the CLI
 47 | 
 48 | ```bash
 49 | python app.py
 50 | ```
 51 | 
 52 | ### Menu Options
 53 | 
 54 | 1. **Analyze Example Code (Buggy Python)**: Demonstrates debugging capabilities with intentionally buggy code
 55 | 2. **Analyze Example Code (Inefficient Python)**: Shows efficiency analysis on O(n²) code
 56 | 3. **Analyze Custom Code**: Submit your own code for analysis
 57 | 4. **View Example Files**: Browse available example code files
 58 | 5. **Check Service Health**: Verify all microservices are running
 59 | 6. **About This System**: Learn about the system architecture and features
 60 | 0. **Exit**: Close the application
 61 | 
 62 | ### Analyzing Custom Code
 63 | 
 64 | When selecting option 3:
 65 | 
 66 | 1. Choose the programming language (Python, C++, or Java)
 67 | 2. Select input method:
 68 |    - Enter code directly (end with Ctrl+D on Unix/Linux or Ctrl+Z on Windows)
 69 |    - Load from a file (provide file path)
 70 | 3. View comprehensive analysis results
 71 | 
 72 | ## Example Files
 73 | 
 74 | The `examples/` directory contains three demonstration files:
 75 | 
 76 | ### buggy_code.py
 77 | Contains multiple intentional bugs:
 78 | - Syntax errors (missing colons)
 79 | - Logic errors (off-by-one errors)
 80 | - Runtime errors (division by zero, index out of bounds)
 81 | 
 82 | ### inefficient_code.py
 83 | Demonstrates inefficient algorithms:
 84 | - O(n²) time complexity with nested loops
 85 | - Inefficient pattern: checking membership in lists
 86 | - Can be optimized to O(n) using hash maps/sets
 87 | 
 88 | ### optimized_code.py
 89 | Shows optimized implementations:
 90 | - O(n) time complexity
 91 | - Efficient use of data structures (sets, dictionaries)
 92 | - Best practices for algorithm design
 93 | 
 94 | ## Output Format
 95 | 
 96 | The CLI displays results in the following structure:
 97 | 
 98 | ```
 99 | === DIAGNOSTIC SUMMARY ===
100 | [Bug descriptions and explanations]
101 | 
102 | === COMPLEXITY BREAKDOWN ===
103 | Current Time Complexity: O(n²)
104 | Current Space Complexity: O(n)
105 | Target Time Complexity: O(n)
106 | Target Space Complexity: O(n)
107 | 
108 | === THE OPTIMIZATION PATH ===
109 | Step 1: [Conceptual guide]
110 | Step 2: [Conceptual guide]
111 | ...
112 | 
113 | === AUTOMATED ACTIONS ===
114 | ✓ Documentation updated: [file paths]
115 | ✓ Tickets created: [ticket IDs]
116 | ✓ Learning path generated: [topics]
117 | 
118 | === REFACTORED CODE ===
119 | [Optimized code with explanation]
120 | ```
121 | 
122 | ## Architecture
123 | 
124 | The CLI application consists of:
125 | 
126 | ```
127 | demo/cli-demo/
128 | ├── app.py                    # Main CLI application
129 | ├── services/
130 | │   ├── __init__.py
131 | │   ├── api_client.py         # API client for microservices
132 | │   └── formatter.py          # Output formatting
133 | ├── examples/
134 | │   ├── buggy_code.py         # Example with bugs
135 | │   ├── inefficient_code.py   # Example with O(n²) complexity
136 | │   └── optimized_code.py     # Optimized O(n) code
137 | ├── requirements.txt
138 | └── README.md
139 | ```
140 | 
141 | ## API Client
142 | 
143 | The `api_client.py` module provides methods to interact with all microservices:
144 | 
145 | - `analyze_debugging()`: Submit code to debugging engine
146 | - `analyze_efficiency()`: Submit code to efficiency analyzer
147 | - `generate_refactored_code()`: Request code refactoring from watsonx.ai
148 | - `trigger_automated_actions()`: Trigger watsonx Orchestrate workflows
149 | - `complete_analysis()`: Perform full analysis pipeline
150 | - `health_check()`: Check service availability
151 | 
152 | ## Troubleshooting
153 | 
154 | ### Services Not Available
155 | 
156 | If you see "Service unavailable" errors:
157 | 
158 | 1. Check that all microservices are running:
159 | ```bash
160 | # Check debugging engine
161 | curl http://localhost:8001/health
162 | 
163 | # Check efficiency analyzer
164 | curl http://localhost:8002/health
165 | 
166 | # Check watsonx.ai integration
167 | curl http://localhost:8003/health
168 | 
169 | # Check watsonx Orchestrate integration
170 | curl http://localhost:8004/health
171 | ```
172 | 
173 | 2. Start any missing services:
174 | ```bash
175 | # Start debugging engine
176 | cd services/debugging-engine
177 | python -m app.main
178 | 
179 | # Start efficiency analyzer
180 | cd services/efficiency-analyzer
181 | python -m app.main
182 | 
183 | # Start watsonx.ai integration
184 | cd services/watsonx-ai-integration
185 | python -m app.handler
186 | 
187 | # Start watsonx Orchestrate integration
188 | cd services/watsonx-orchestrate-integration
189 | python -m app.handler
190 | ```
191 | 
192 | ### Import Errors
193 | 
194 | If you encounter import errors:
195 | 
196 | ```bash
197 | # Ensure you're in the correct directory
198 | cd demo/cli-demo
199 | 
200 | # Reinstall dependencies
201 | pip install -r requirements.txt
202 | ```
203 | 
204 | ### Color Display Issues on Windows
205 | 
206 | If colors don't display correctly on Windows:
207 | 
208 | ```bash
209 | # Colorama should handle this automatically, but if issues persist:
210 | pip install --upgrade colorama
211 | ```
212 | 
213 | ## Development
214 | 
215 | ### Adding New Examples
216 | 
217 | To add new example files:
218 | 
219 | 1. Create a new file in `examples/` directory
220 | 2. Add appropriate comments explaining the issues
221 | 3. Update the CLI menu if needed
222 | 
223 | ### Customizing Output Format
224 | 
225 | Modify `services/formatter.py` to customize:
226 | - Color schemes
227 | - Output structure
228 | - Display formatting
229 | 
230 | ### Extending API Client
231 | 
232 | Add new methods to `services/api_client.py` to support:
233 | - Additional endpoints
234 | - New analysis types
235 | - Custom workflows
236 | 
237 | ## Related Documentation
238 | 
239 | - [Project Summary](../../PROJECT_SUMMARY.md)
240 | - [Getting Started Guide](../../GETTING_STARTED.md)
241 | - [API Reference](../../API_REFERENCE.md)
242 | - [Architecture Documentation](../../ARCHITECTURE.md)
243 | 
244 | ## Support
245 | 
246 | For issues or questions:
247 | - Check the main project README
248 | - Review service-specific documentation
249 | - Verify all services are running and accessible
250 | 
251 | ## License
252 | 
253 | Part of the Algorithmic Debugging & Efficiency Coach project.
</content>

 15 |     SyntaxError as SyntaxErrorModel,
 16 |     LogicError as LogicErrorModel,
 17 |     RootCause as RootCauseModel,
 18 |     Explanation as ExplanationModel
 19 | )
 20 | from .services.execution_flow import ExecutionFlowAnalyzer
 21 | from .services.root_cause import RootCauseIdentifier
 22 | from .services.explainer import BugExplainer
 23 | from .parsers import PythonParser, CppParser, JavaParser
 24 | from .utils.logger import get_logger
 25 | 
 26 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 27 | 
 28 | # Initialize FastAPI app
 29 | app = FastAPI(
 30 |     title="Debugging Engine Service",
 31 |     description="Analyzes code submissions, diagnoses bugs, and provides plain-language explanations",
 32 |     version="1.0.0",
 33 |     docs_url="/docs",
 34 |     redoc_url="/redoc"
 35 | )
 36 | 
 37 | # Add CORS middleware
 38 | app.add_middleware(
 39 |     CORSMiddleware,
 40 |     allow_origins=["*"],  # Configure appropriately for production
 41 |     allow_credentials=True,
 42 |     allow_methods=["*"],
 43 |     allow_headers=["*"],
 44 | )
 45 | 
 46 | # Initialize services
 47 | execution_flow_analyzer = ExecutionFlowAnalyzer()
 48 | root_cause_identifier = RootCauseIdentifier()
 49 | bug_explainer = BugExplainer()
 50 | 
 51 | 
 52 | @app.get("/health", status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)
 53 | async def health_check():
 54 |     """
 55 |     Health check endpoint
 56 |     
 57 |     Returns:
 58 |         Health status of the service
 59 |     """
 60 |     return {
 61 |         "status": "healthy",
 62 |         "service": "debugging-engine",
 63 |         "version": "1.0.0"
 64 |     }
 65 | 
 66 | 
 67 | @app.post("/api/v1/debug", response_model=DebugReport, status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)
 68 | async def debug_code(submission: CodeSubmission):
 69 |     """
 70 |     Analyze code submission and provide debugging report
 71 |     
 72 |     Args:
 73 |         submission: Code submission with language and code
 74 |         
 75 |     Returns:
 76 |         Comprehensive debugging report
 77 |         
 78 |     Raises:
 79 |         HTTPException: If analysis fails
 80 |     """
 81 |     start_time = time.time()
 82 |     
 83 |     logger.info(f"Received debug request for {submission.language} code")
 84 |     
 85 |     try:
 86 |         # Step 1: Parse the code
 87 |         logger.info("Step 1: Parsing code")
 88 |         parsed_data = await _parse_code(submission.code, submission.language)
 89 |         
 90 |         # Step 2: Analyze execution flow
 91 |         logger.info("Step 2: Analyzing execution flow")
 92 |         execution_flow_data = execution_flow_analyzer.analyze(
 93 |             submission.code, 
 94 |             submission.language
 95 |         )
 96 |         
 97 |         # Step 3: Identify root causes
 98 |         logger.info("Step 3: Identifying root causes")
 99 |         root_cause_data = root_cause_identifier.identify(
100 |             submission.code,
101 |             submission.language,
102 |             parsed_data
103 |         )
104 |         
105 |         # Step 4: Generate explanations
106 |         logger.info("Step 4: Generating explanations")
107 |         explanations = bug_explainer.explain(
108 |             root_cause_data.get('syntax_errors', []),
109 |             root_cause_data.get('logic_errors', []),
110 |             root_cause_data.get('root_causes', [])
111 |         )
112 |         
113 |         # Calculate analysis time
114 |         analysis_time = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000  # Convert to milliseconds
115 |         
116 |         # Build response
117 |         has_errors = (
118 |             len(root_cause_data.get('syntax_errors', [])) > 0 or
119 |             len(root_cause_data.get('logic_errors', [])) > 0
120 |         )
121 |         
122 |         # Create ExecutionFlow object
123 |         exec_flow = ExecutionFlow(
124 |             entry_point=execution_flow_data.get('entry_point'),
125 |             functions=execution_flow_data.get('functions', []),
126 |             control_structures=execution_flow_data.get('control_structures', []),
127 |             call_graph=execution_flow_data.get('call_graph', {}),
128 |             unreachable_code=execution_flow_data.get('unreachable_code', [])
129 |         )
130 |         
131 |         # Convert dictionaries to Pydantic models
132 |         syntax_error_models = [SyntaxErrorModel(**err) for err in root_cause_data.get('syntax_errors', [])]
133 |         logic_error_models = [LogicErrorModel(**err) for err in root_cause_data.get('logic_errors', [])]
134 |         root_cause_models = [RootCauseModel(**rc) for rc in root_cause_data.get('root_causes', [])]
135 |         explanation_models = [ExplanationModel(**exp) for exp in explanations]
136 |         
137 |         report = DebugReport(
138 |             has_errors=has_errors,
139 |             syntax_errors=syntax_error_models,
140 |             logic_errors=logic_error_models,
141 |             execution_flow=exec_flow,
142 |             root_causes=root_cause_models,
143 |             explanations=explanation_models,
144 |             analysis_time_ms=analysis_time
145 |         )
146 |         
147 |         logger.info(f"Analysis completed in {analysis_time:.2f}ms")
148 |         return report
149 |         
150 |     except Exception as e:
151 |         logger.error(f"Error during code analysis: {e}", exc_info=True)
152 |         raise HTTPException(
153 |             status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
154 |             detail=f"Failed to analyze code: {str(e)}"
155 |         )
156 | 
157 | 
158 | async def _parse_code(code: str, language) -> dict:
159 |     """
160 |     Parse code using appropriate parser
161 |     
162 |     Args:
163 |         code: Source code
164 |         language: Programming language
165 |         
166 |     Returns:
167 |         Parsed code structure
168 |     """
169 |     from .models.request import ProgrammingLanguage
170 |     
171 |     if language == ProgrammingLanguage.PYTHON:
172 |         parser = PythonParser()
173 |     elif language == ProgrammingLanguage.CPP:
174 |         parser = CppParser()
175 |     elif language == ProgrammingLanguage.JAVA:
176 |         parser = JavaParser()
177 |     else:
178 |         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported language: {language}")
179 |     
180 |     return parser.parse(code)
181 | 
182 | 
183 | @app.exception_handler(HTTPException)
184 | async def http_exception_handler(request, exc):
185 |     """Custom HTTP exception handler"""
186 |     return JSONResponse(
187 |         status_code=exc.status_code,
188 |         content={
189 |             "error": exc.detail,
190 |             "status_code": exc.status_code
191 |         }
192 |     )
193 | 
194 | 
195 | @app.exception_handler(Exception)
196 | async def general_exception_handler(request, exc):
197 |     """General exception handler"""
198 |     logger.error(f"Unhandled exception: {exc}", exc_info=True)
199 |     return JSONResponse(
200 |         status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
201 |         content={
202 |             "error": "Internal server error",
203 |             "detail": str(exc)
204 |         }
205 |     )
206 | 
207 | 
208 | if __name__ == "__main__":

26 |     language: ProgrammingLanguage = Field(
27 |         ...,

29 |     )

31 |         ...,

34 |         description="Source code to analyze"

  9 | class SyntaxError(BaseModel):

 16 |         message: Error message

 18 |     """
 19 |     line: int = Field(..., description="Line number of the error")
 20 |     column: Optional[int] = Field(None, description="Column number of the error")
 21 |     message: str = Field(..., description="Error message")
 22 |     code_snippet: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Code snippet with error context")
 23 |     severity: str = Field(default="error", description="Severity level: error, warning")
 24 | 
 25 | 
 26 | class LogicError(BaseModel):
 27 |     """
 28 |     Model for logic errors
 29 |     
 30 |     Attributes:
 31 |         type: Type of logic error (e.g., infinite_loop, null_pointer, type_mismatch)
 32 |         line: Line number where the error occurs

 1 | """
 2 | Logging configuration for the Debugging Engine service
 3 | """
 4 | 
 5 | import logging
 6 | import sys
 7 | from typing import Optional
 8 | 
 9 | 
10 | def get_logger(name: Optional[str] = None) -> logging.Logger:
11 |     """
12 |     Get a configured logger instance
13 |     
14 |     Args:
15 |         name: Logger name (defaults to root logger if None)
16 |         
17 |     Returns:
18 |         Configured logger instance
19 |     """
20 |     logger = logging.getLogger(name or __name__)
21 |     
22 |     # Only configure if no handlers exist (avoid duplicate handlers)
23 |     if not logger.handlers:
24 |         # Set log level
25 |         logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
26 |         
27 |         # Create console handler
28 |         console_handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
29 |         console_handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)
30 |         
31 |         # Create formatter
32 |         formatter = logging.Formatter(
33 |             fmt='%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s',
34 |             datefmt='%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'
35 |         )
36 |         console_handler.setFormatter(formatter)
37 |         
38 |         # Add handler to logger
39 |         logger.addHandler(console_handler)
40 |     
41 |     return logger
42 | 
43 | 
44 | # Create a default logger for the module
45 | logger = get_logger("debugging-engine")
46 |

  1 | """
  2 | Python code parser using built-in ast module
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | import ast
  6 | from typing import Dict, List, Any, Optional
  7 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
  8 | 
  9 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 10 | 
 11 | 
 12 | class PythonParser:
 13 |     """
 14 |     Parser for Python code using the built-in ast module
 15 |     """
 16 |     
 17 |     def __init__(self):
 18 |         """Initialize the Python parser"""
 19 |         self.tree: Optional[ast.AST] = None
 20 |         self.source_lines: List[str] = []
 21 |     
 22 |     def parse(self, code: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 23 |         """
 24 |         Parse Python code and extract structural information
 25 |         
 26 |         Args:
 27 |             code: Python source code as string
 28 |             
 29 |         Returns:
 30 |             Dictionary containing parsed information
 31 |             
 32 |         Raises:
 33 |             SyntaxError: If the code has syntax errors
 34 |         """
 35 |         self.source_lines = code.split('\n')
 36 |         
 37 |         try:
 38 |             self.tree = ast.parse(code)
 39 |             
 40 |             return {
 41 |                 'success': True,
 42 |                 'functions': self._extract_functions(),
 43 |                 'classes': self._extract_classes(),
 44 |                 'imports': self._extract_imports(),
 45 |                 'variables': self._extract_variables(),
 46 |                 'control_structures': self._extract_control_structures(),
 47 |                 'syntax_errors': []
 48 |             }
 49 |         except SyntaxError as e:
 50 |             logger.error(f"Syntax error in Python code: {e}")
 51 |             return {
 52 |                 'success': False,
 53 |                 'functions': [],
 54 |                 'classes': [],
 55 |                 'imports': [],
 56 |                 'variables': [],
 57 |                 'control_structures': [],
 58 |                 'syntax_errors': [{
 59 |                     'line': e.lineno or 0,
 60 |                     'column': e.offset or 0,
 61 |                     'message': str(e.msg),
 62 |                     'text': e.text or ''
 63 |                 }]
 64 |             }
 65 |     
 66 |     def _extract_functions(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
 67 |         """Extract function definitions from the AST"""
 68 |         functions = []
 69 |         
 70 |         if not self.tree:
 71 |             return functions
 72 |         
 73 |         for node in ast.walk(self.tree):
 74 |             if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef):
 75 |                 functions.append({
 76 |                     'name': node.name,
 77 |                     'line': node.lineno,
 78 |                     'end_line': node.end_lineno,
 79 |                     'params': [arg.arg for arg in node.args.args],
 80 |                     'decorators': [self._get_decorator_name(d) for d in node.decorator_list],
 81 |                     'is_async': False
 82 |                 })
 83 |             elif isinstance(node, ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
 84 |                 functions.append({
 85 |                     'name': node.name,
 86 |                     'line': node.lineno,
 87 |                     'end_line': node.end_lineno,
 88 |                     'params': [arg.arg for arg in node.args.args],
 89 |                     'decorators': [self._get_decorator_name(d) for d in node.decorator_list],
 90 |                     'is_async': True
 91 |                 })
 92 |         
 93 |         return functions
 94 |     
 95 |     def _extract_classes(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
 96 |         """Extract class definitions from the AST"""
 97 |         classes = []
 98 |         
 99 |         if not self.tree:
100 |             return classes
101 |         
102 |         for node in ast.walk(self.tree):
103 |             if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
104 |                 methods = []
105 |                 for item in node.body:
106 |                     if isinstance(item, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
107 |                         methods.append(item.name)
108 |                 
109 |                 classes.append({
110 |                     'name': node.name,
111 |                     'line': node.lineno,
112 |                     'end_line': node.end_lineno,
113 |                     'bases': [self._get_name(base) for base in node.bases],
114 |                     'methods': methods,
115 |                     'decorators': [self._get_decorator_name(d) for d in node.decorator_list]
116 |                 })
117 |         
118 |         return classes
119 |     
120 |     def _extract_imports(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
121 |         """Extract import statements from the AST"""
122 |         imports = []
123 |         
124 |         if not self.tree:
125 |             return imports
126 |         
127 |         for node in ast.walk(self.tree):
128 |             if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
129 |                 for alias in node.names:
130 |                     imports.append({
131 |                         'type': 'import',
132 |                         'module': alias.name,
133 |                         'alias': alias.asname,
134 |                         'line': node.lineno
135 |                     })
136 |             elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
137 |                 for alias in node.names:
138 |                     imports.append({
139 |                         'type': 'from_import',
140 |                         'module': node.module or '',
141 |                         'name': alias.name,
142 |                         'alias': alias.asname,
143 |                         'line': node.lineno
144 |                     })
145 |         
146 |         return imports
147 |     
148 |     def _extract_variables(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
149 |         """Extract variable assignments from the AST"""
150 |         variables = []
151 |         
152 |         if not self.tree:
153 |             return variables
154 |         
155 |         for node in ast.walk(self.tree):
156 |             if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
157 |                 for target in node.targets:
158 |                     if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
159 |                         variables.append({
160 |                             'name': target.id,
161 |                             'line': node.lineno,
162 |                             'scope': 'global'  # Simplified; would need scope analysis
163 |                         })
164 |         
165 |         return variables
166 |     
167 |     def _extract_control_structures(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
168 |         """Extract control flow structures (if, for, while, etc.)"""
169 |         structures = []
170 |         
171 |         if not self.tree:
172 |             return structures
173 |         
174 |         for node in ast.walk(self.tree):
175 |             if isinstance(node, ast.If):
176 |                 structures.append({
177 |                     'type': 'if',
178 |                     'line': node.lineno,
179 |                     'end_line': node.end_lineno,
180 |                     'has_else': len(node.orelse) > 0
181 |                 })
182 |             elif isinstance(node, ast.For):
183 |                 structures.append({
184 |                     'type': 'for',
185 |                     'line': node.lineno,
186 |                     'end_line': node.end_lineno,
187 |                     'target': self._get_name(node.target),
188 |                     'has_else': len(node.orelse) > 0
189 |                 })
190 |             elif isinstance(node, ast.While):
191 |                 structures.append({
192 |                     'type': 'while',
193 |                     'line': node.lineno,
194 |                     'end_line': node.end_lineno,
195 |                     'has_else': len(node.orelse) > 0
196 |                 })
197 |             elif isinstance(node, ast.Try):
198 |                 structures.append({
199 |                     'type': 'try',
200 |                     'line': node.lineno,
201 |                     'end_line': node.end_lineno,
202 |                     'handlers': len(node.handlers),
203 |                     'has_finally': len(node.finalbody) > 0
204 |                 })
205 |         
206 |         return structures
207 |     
208 |     def _get_name(self, node: ast.AST) -> str:
209 |         """Get the name from an AST node"""
210 |         if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
211 |             return node.id
212 |         elif isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
213 |             return f"{self._get_name(node.value)}.{node.attr}"
214 |         return str(node)
215 |     
216 |     def _get_decorator_name(self, node: ast.AST) -> str:
217 |         """Get decorator name from AST node"""
218 |         if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
219 |             return node.id
220 |         elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
221 |             return self._get_name(node.func)
222 |         return str(node)
223 | 
224 | # Made with Bob

<content lines="1-316">
  1 | """
  2 | C++ code parser using tree-sitter
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | from typing import Dict, List, Any, Optional
  6 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
  7 | 
  8 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
  9 | 
 10 | try:
 11 |     from tree_sitter import Language, Parser
 12 |     import tree_sitter_cpp as tscpp
 13 |     TREE_SITTER_AVAILABLE = True
 14 | except ImportError:
 15 |     TREE_SITTER_AVAILABLE = False
 16 |     logger.warning("tree-sitter not available, C++ parsing will be limited")
 17 | 
 18 | 
 19 | class CppParser:
 20 |     """
 21 |     Parser for C++ code using tree-sitter
 22 |     """
 23 |     
 24 |     def __init__(self):
 25 |         """Initialize the C++ parser"""
 26 |         self.parser: Optional[Any] = None
 27 |         self.tree: Optional[Any] = None
 28 |         self.source_code: str = ""
 29 |         
 30 |         if TREE_SITTER_AVAILABLE:
 31 |             try:
 32 |                 CPP_LANGUAGE = Language(tscpp.language())
 33 |                 self.parser = Parser(CPP_LANGUAGE)
 34 |             except Exception as e:
 35 |                 logger.error(f"Failed to initialize C++ parser: {e}")
 36 |                 self.parser = None
 37 |     
 38 |     def parse(self, code: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 39 |         """
 40 |         Parse C++ code and extract structural information
 41 |         
 42 |         Args:
 43 |             code: C++ source code as string
 44 |             
 45 |         Returns:
 46 |             Dictionary containing parsed information
 47 |         """
 48 |         self.source_code = code
 49 |         
 50 |         if not TREE_SITTER_AVAILABLE or not self.parser:
 51 |             return self._fallback_parse(code)
 52 |         
 53 |         try:
 54 |             self.tree = self.parser.parse(bytes(code, "utf8"))
 55 |             
 56 |             return {
 57 |                 'success': True,
 58 |                 'functions': self._extract_functions(),
 59 |                 'classes': self._extract_classes(),
 60 |                 'includes': self._extract_includes(),
 61 |                 'variables': self._extract_variables(),
 62 |                 'control_structures': self._extract_control_structures(),
 63 |                 'syntax_errors': self._check_syntax_errors()
 64 |             }
 65 |         except Exception as e:
 66 |             logger.error(f"Error parsing C++ code: {e}")
 67 |             return {
 68 |                 'success': False,
 69 |                 'functions': [],
 70 |                 'classes': [],
 71 |                 'includes': [],
 72 |                 'variables': [],
 73 |                 'control_structures': [],
 74 |                 'syntax_errors': [{'message': str(e), 'line': 0}]
 75 |             }
 76 |     
 77 |     def _fallback_parse(self, code: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 78 |         """Fallback parsing using simple regex patterns"""
 79 |         import re
 80 |         
 81 |         functions = []
 82 |         classes = []
 83 |         includes = []
 84 |         
 85 |         # Extract includes
 86 |         for match in re.finditer(r'#include\s*[<"]([^>"]+)[>"]', code):
 87 |             includes.append({
 88 |                 'file': match.group(1),
 89 |                 'line': code[:match.start()].count('\n') + 1
 90 |             })
 91 |         
 92 |         # Extract function declarations (simplified)
 93 |         for match in re.finditer(r'(\w+)\s+(\w+)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*{', code):
 94 |             functions.append({
 95 |                 'return_type': match.group(1),
 96 |                 'name': match.group(2),
 97 |                 'line': code[:match.start()].count('\n') + 1
 98 |             })
 99 |         
100 |         # Extract class declarations
101 |         for match in re.finditer(r'class\s+(\w+)', code):
102 |             classes.append({
103 |                 'name': match.group(1),
104 |                 'line': code[:match.start()].count('\n') + 1
105 |             })
106 |         
107 |         return {
108 |             'success': True,
109 |             'functions': functions,
110 |             'classes': classes,
111 |             'includes': includes,
112 |             'variables': [],
113 |             'control_structures': [],
114 |             'syntax_errors': []
115 |         }
116 |     
117 |     def _extract_functions(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
118 |         """Extract function definitions from the parse tree"""
119 |         if not self.tree:
120 |             return []
121 |         
122 |         functions = []
123 |         
124 |         def traverse(node):
125 |             if node.type == 'function_definition':
126 |                 func_info = self._parse_function_node(node)
127 |                 if func_info:
128 |                     functions.append(func_info)
129 |             
130 |             for child in node.children:
131 |                 traverse(child)
132 |         
133 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
134 |         return functions
135 |     
136 |     def _extract_classes(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
137 |         """Extract class definitions from the parse tree"""
138 |         if not self.tree:
139 |             return []
140 |         
141 |         classes = []
142 |         
143 |         def traverse(node):
144 |             if node.type in ('class_specifier', 'struct_specifier'):
145 |                 class_info = self._parse_class_node(node)
146 |                 if class_info:
147 |                     classes.append(class_info)
148 |             
149 |             for child in node.children:
150 |                 traverse(child)
151 |         
152 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
153 |         return classes
154 |     
155 |     def _extract_includes(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
156 |         """Extract include directives"""
157 |         if not self.tree:
158 |             return []
159 |         
160 |         includes = []
161 |         
162 |         def traverse(node):
163 |             if node.type == 'preproc_include':
164 |                 include_info = self._parse_include_node(node)
165 |                 if include_info:
166 |                     includes.append(include_info)
167 |             
168 |             for child in node.children:
169 |                 traverse(child)
170 |         
171 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
172 |         return includes
173 |     
174 |     def _extract_variables(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
175 |         """Extract variable declarations"""
176 |         if not self.tree:
177 |             return []
178 |         
179 |         variables = []
180 |         
181 |         def traverse(node):
182 |             if node.type == 'declaration':
183 |                 var_info = self._parse_variable_node(node)
184 |                 if var_info:
185 |                     variables.extend(var_info)
186 |             
187 |             for child in node.children:
188 |                 traverse(child)
189 |         
190 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
191 |         return variables
192 |     
193 |     def _extract_control_structures(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
194 |         """Extract control flow structures"""
195 |         if not self.tree:
196 |             return []
197 |         
198 |         structures = []
199 |         
200 |         def traverse(node):
201 |             if node.type in ('if_statement', 'for_statement', 'while_statement', 
202 |                            'do_statement', 'switch_statement'):
203 |                 structures.append({
204 |                     'type': node.type.replace('_statement', ''),
205 |                     'line': node.start_point[0] + 1,
206 |                     'end_line': node.end_point[0] + 1
207 |                 })
208 |             
209 |             for child in node.children:
210 |                 traverse(child)
211 |         
212 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
213 |         return structures
214 |     
215 |     def _check_syntax_errors(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
216 |         """Check for syntax errors in the parse tree"""
217 |         if not self.tree:
218 |             return []
219 |         
220 |         errors = []
221 |         
222 |         def traverse(node):
223 |             if node.type == 'ERROR' or node.is_missing:
224 |                 errors.append({
225 |                     'line': node.start_point[0] + 1,
226 |                     'column': node.start_point[1] + 1,
227 |                     'message': f"Syntax error at {node.type}",
228 |                     'text': self._get_node_text(node)
229 |                 })
230 |             
231 |             for child in node.children:
232 |                 traverse(child)
233 |         
234 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
235 |         return errors
236 |     
237 |     def _parse_function_node(self, node) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
238 |         """Parse a function definition node"""
239 |         try:
240 |             return {
241 |                 'name': self._get_function_name(node),
242 |                 'line': node.start_point[0] + 1,
243 |                 'end_line': node.end_point[0] + 1,
244 |                 'return_type': self._get_return_type(node)
245 |             }
246 |         except Exception as e:
247 |             logger.debug(f"Error parsing function node: {e}")
248 |             return None
249 |     
250 |     def _parse_class_node(self, node) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
251 |         """Parse a class definition node"""
252 |         try:
253 |             return {
254 |                 'name': self._get_class_name(node),
255 |                 'line': node.start_point[0] + 1,
256 |                 'end_line': node.end_point[0] + 1,
257 |                 'type': 'class' if node.type == 'class_specifier' else 'struct'
258 |             }
259 |         except Exception as e:
260 |             logger.debug(f"Error parsing class node: {e}")
261 |             return None
262 |     
263 |     def _parse_include_node(self, node) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
264 |         """Parse an include directive node"""
265 |         try:
266 |             text = self._get_node_text(node)
267 |             return {
268 |                 'file': text,
269 |                 'line': node.start_point[0] + 1
270 |             }
271 |         except Exception as e:
272 |             logger.debug(f"Error parsing include node: {e}")
273 |             return None
274 |     
275 |     def _parse_variable_node(self, node) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
276 |         """Parse variable declaration nodes"""
277 |         variables = []
278 |         try:
279 |             for child in node.children:
280 |                 if child.type == 'init_declarator':
281 |                     variables.append({
282 |                         'name': self._get_node_text(child),
283 |                         'line': child.start_point[0] + 1
284 |                     })
285 |         except Exception as e:
286 |             logger.debug(f"Error parsing variable node: {e}")
287 |         return variables
288 |     
289 |     def _get_node_text(self, node) -> str:
290 |         """Get the text content of a node"""
291 |         return self.source_code[node.start_byte:node.end_byte]
292 |     
293 |     def _get_function_name(self, node) -> str:
294 |         """Extract function name from function definition node"""
295 |         for child in node.children:
296 |             if child.type == 'function_declarator':
297 |                 for subchild in child.children:
298 |                     if subchild.type == 'identifier':
299 |                         return self._get_node_text(subchild)
300 |         return "unknown"
301 |     
302 |     def _get_class_name(self, node) -> str:
303 |         """Extract class name from class definition node"""
304 |         for child in node.children:
305 |             if child.type == 'type_identifier':
306 |                 return self._get_node_text(child)
307 |         return "unknown"
308 |     
309 |     def _get_return_type(self, node) -> str:
310 |         """Extract return type from function definition node"""
311 |         for child in node.children:
312 |             if child.type in ('primitive_type', 'type_identifier'):
313 |                 return self._get_node_text(child)
314 |         return "void"
315 | 
316 | # Made with Bob
</content>
