  1 | """
  2 | Java code parser using tree-sitter
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | from typing import Dict, List, Any, Optional
  6 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
  7 | 
  8 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
  9 | 
 10 | try:
 11 |     from tree_sitter import Language, Parser
 12 |     import tree_sitter_java as tsjava
 13 |     TREE_SITTER_AVAILABLE = True
 14 | except ImportError:
 15 |     TREE_SITTER_AVAILABLE = False
 16 |     logger.warning("tree-sitter not available, Java parsing will be limited")
 17 | 
 18 | 
 19 | class JavaParser:
 20 |     """
 21 |     Parser for Java code using tree-sitter
 22 |     """
 23 |     
 24 |     def __init__(self):
 25 |         """Initialize the Java parser"""
 26 |         self.parser: Optional[Any] = None
 27 |         self.tree: Optional[Any] = None
 28 |         self.source_code: str = ""
 29 |         
 30 |         if TREE_SITTER_AVAILABLE:
 31 |             try:
 32 |                 JAVA_LANGUAGE = Language(tsjava.language())
 33 |                 self.parser = Parser(JAVA_LANGUAGE)
 34 |             except Exception as e:
 35 |                 logger.error(f"Failed to initialize Java parser: {e}")
 36 |                 self.parser = None
 37 |     
 38 |     def parse(self, code: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 39 |         """
 40 |         Parse Java code and extract structural information
 41 |         
 42 |         Args:
 43 |             code: Java source code as string
 44 |             
 45 |         Returns:
 46 |             Dictionary containing parsed information
 47 |         """
 48 |         self.source_code = code
 49 |         
 50 |         if not TREE_SITTER_AVAILABLE or not self.parser:
 51 |             return self._fallback_parse(code)
 52 |         
 53 |         try:
 54 |             self.tree = self.parser.parse(bytes(code, "utf8"))
 55 |             
 56 |             return {
 57 |                 'success': True,
 58 |                 'functions': self._extract_methods(),
 59 |                 'classes': self._extract_classes(),
 60 |                 'imports': self._extract_imports(),
 61 |                 'variables': self._extract_fields(),
 62 |                 'control_structures': self._extract_control_structures(),
 63 |                 'syntax_errors': self._check_syntax_errors()
 64 |             }
 65 |         except Exception as e:
 66 |             logger.error(f"Error parsing Java code: {e}")
 67 |             return {
 68 |                 'success': False,
 69 |                 'functions': [],
 70 |                 'classes': [],
 71 |                 'imports': [],
 72 |                 'variables': [],
 73 |                 'control_structures': [],
 74 |                 'syntax_errors': [{'message': str(e), 'line': 0}]
 75 |             }
 76 |     
 77 |     def _fallback_parse(self, code: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 78 |         """Fallback parsing using simple regex patterns"""
 79 |         import re
 80 |         
 81 |         methods = []
 82 |         classes = []
 83 |         imports = []
 84 |         
 85 |         # Extract imports
 86 |         for match in re.finditer(r'import\s+([\w.]+);', code):
 87 |             imports.append({
 88 |                 'package': match.group(1),
 89 |                 'line': code[:match.start()].count('\n') + 1
 90 |             })
 91 |         
 92 |         # Extract class declarations
 93 |         for match in re.finditer(r'(?:public\s+)?class\s+(\w+)', code):
 94 |             classes.append({
 95 |                 'name': match.group(1),
 96 |                 'line': code[:match.start()].count('\n') + 1
 97 |             })
 98 |         
 99 |         # Extract method declarations (simplified)
100 |         for match in re.finditer(r'(?:public|private|protected)?\s*(?:static\s+)?(\w+)\s+(\w+)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*{', code):
101 |             methods.append({
102 |                 'return_type': match.group(1),
103 |                 'name': match.group(2),
104 |                 'line': code[:match.start()].count('\n') + 1
105 |             })
106 |         
107 |         return {
108 |             'success': True,
109 |             'functions': methods,
110 |             'classes': classes,
111 |             'imports': imports,
112 |             'variables': [],
113 |             'control_structures': [],
114 |             'syntax_errors': []
115 |         }
116 |     
117 |     def _extract_methods(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
118 |         """Extract method definitions from the parse tree"""
119 |         if not self.tree:
120 |             return []
121 |         
122 |         methods = []
123 |         
124 |         def traverse(node):
125 |             if node.type == 'method_declaration':
126 |                 method_info = self._parse_method_node(node)
127 |                 if method_info:
128 |                     methods.append(method_info)
129 |             
130 |             for child in node.children:
131 |                 traverse(child)
132 |         
133 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
134 |         return methods
135 |     
136 |     def _extract_classes(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
137 |         """Extract class definitions from the parse tree"""
138 |         if not self.tree:
139 |             return []
140 |         
141 |         classes = []
142 |         
143 |         def traverse(node):
144 |             if node.type in ('class_declaration', 'interface_declaration'):
145 |                 class_info = self._parse_class_node(node)
146 |                 if class_info:
147 |                     classes.append(class_info)
148 |             
149 |             for child in node.children:
150 |                 traverse(child)
151 |         
152 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
153 |         return classes
154 |     
155 |     def _extract_imports(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
156 |         """Extract import statements"""
157 |         if not self.tree:
158 |             return []
159 |         
160 |         imports = []
161 |         
162 |         def traverse(node):
163 |             if node.type == 'import_declaration':
164 |                 import_info = self._parse_import_node(node)
165 |                 if import_info:
166 |                     imports.append(import_info)
167 |             
168 |             for child in node.children:
169 |                 traverse(child)
170 |         
171 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
172 |         return imports
173 |     
174 |     def _extract_fields(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
175 |         """Extract field declarations"""
176 |         if not self.tree:
177 |             return []
178 |         
179 |         fields = []
180 |         
181 |         def traverse(node):
182 |             if node.type == 'field_declaration':
183 |                 field_info = self._parse_field_node(node)
184 |                 if field_info:
185 |                     fields.extend(field_info)
186 |             
187 |             for child in node.children:
188 |                 traverse(child)
189 |         
190 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
191 |         return fields
192 |     
193 |     def _extract_control_structures(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
194 |         """Extract control flow structures"""
195 |         if not self.tree:
196 |             return []
197 |         
198 |         structures = []
199 |         
200 |         def traverse(node):
201 |             if node.type in ('if_statement', 'for_statement', 'while_statement',
202 |                            'do_statement', 'switch_expression', 'enhanced_for_statement'):
203 |                 structures.append({
204 |                     'type': node.type.replace('_statement', '').replace('_expression', ''),
205 |                     'line': node.start_point[0] + 1,
206 |                     'end_line': node.end_point[0] + 1
207 |                 })
208 |             
209 |             for child in node.children:
210 |                 traverse(child)
211 |         
212 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
213 |         return structures
214 |     
215 |     def _check_syntax_errors(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
216 |         """Check for syntax errors in the parse tree"""
217 |         if not self.tree:
218 |             return []
219 |         
220 |         errors = []
221 |         
222 |         def traverse(node):
223 |             if node.type == 'ERROR' or node.is_missing:
224 |                 errors.append({
225 |                     'line': node.start_point[0] + 1,
226 |                     'column': node.start_point[1] + 1,
227 |                     'message': f"Syntax error at {node.type}",
228 |                     'text': self._get_node_text(node)
229 |                 })
230 |             
231 |             for child in node.children:
232 |                 traverse(child)
233 |         
234 |         traverse(self.tree.root_node)
235 |         return errors
236 |     
237 |     def _parse_method_node(self, node) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
238 |         """Parse a method declaration node"""
239 |         try:
240 |             return {
241 |                 'name': self._get_method_name(node),
242 |                 'line': node.start_point[0] + 1,
243 |                 'end_line': node.end_point[0] + 1,
244 |                 'return_type': self._get_return_type(node),
245 |                 'modifiers': self._get_modifiers(node)
246 |             }
247 |         except Exception as e:
248 |             logger.debug(f"Error parsing method node: {e}")
249 |             return None
250 |     
251 |     def _parse_class_node(self, node) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
252 |         """Parse a class declaration node"""
253 |         try:
254 |             return {
255 |                 'name': self._get_class_name(node),
256 |                 'line': node.start_point[0] + 1,
257 |                 'end_line': node.end_point[0] + 1,
258 |                 'type': 'interface' if node.type == 'interface_declaration' else 'class',
259 |                 'modifiers': self._get_modifiers(node)
260 |             }
261 |         except Exception as e:
262 |             logger.debug(f"Error parsing class node: {e}")
263 |             return None
264 |     
265 |     def _parse_import_node(self, node) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
266 |         """Parse an import declaration node"""
267 |         try:
268 |             text = self._get_node_text(node)
269 |             return {
270 |                 'package': text.replace('import', '').replace(';', '').strip(),
271 |                 'line': node.start_point[0] + 1
272 |             }
273 |         except Exception as e:
274 |             logger.debug(f"Error parsing import node: {e}")
275 |             return None
276 |     
277 |     def _parse_field_node(self, node) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
278 |         """Parse field declaration nodes"""
279 |         fields = []
280 |         try:
281 |             for child in node.children:
282 |                 if child.type == 'variable_declarator':
283 |                     for subchild in child.children:
284 |                         if subchild.type == 'identifier':
285 |                             fields.append({
286 |                                 'name': self._get_node_text(subchild),
287 |                                 'line': child.start_point[0] + 1
288 |                             })
289 |         except Exception as e:
290 |             logger.debug(f"Error parsing field node: {e}")
291 |         return fields
292 |     
293 |     def _get_node_text(self, node) -> str:
294 |         """Get the text content of a node"""
295 |         return self.source_code[node.start_byte:node.end_byte]
296 |     
297 |     def _get_method_name(self, node) -> str:
298 |         """Extract method name from method declaration node"""
299 |         for child in node.children:
300 |             if child.type == 'identifier':
301 |                 return self._get_node_text(child)
302 |         return "unknown"
303 |     
304 |     def _get_class_name(self, node) -> str:
305 |         """Extract class name from class declaration node"""
306 |         for child in node.children:
307 |             if child.type == 'identifier':
308 |                 return self._get_node_text(child)
309 |         return "unknown"
310 |     
311 |     def _get_return_type(self, node) -> str:
312 |         """Extract return type from method declaration node"""
313 |         for child in node.children:
314 |             if child.type in ('type_identifier', 'void_type', 'integral_type'):
315 |                 return self._get_node_text(child)
316 |         return "void"
317 |     
318 |     def _get_modifiers(self, node) -> List[str]:
319 |         """Extract modifiers from a declaration node"""
320 |         modifiers = []
321 |         for child in node.children:
322 |             if child.type == 'modifiers':
323 |                 for modifier in child.children:
324 |                     modifiers.append(self._get_node_text(modifier))
325 |         return modifiers

  1 | """
  2 | Execution Flow Analyzer
  3 | Analyzes code execution paths and control flow
  4 | """
  5 | 
  6 | from typing import Dict, List, Any
  7 | from ..models.request import ProgrammingLanguage
  8 | from ..parsers import PythonParser, CppParser, JavaParser
  9 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
 10 | 
 11 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 12 | 
 13 | 
 14 | class ExecutionFlowAnalyzer:
 15 |     """
 16 |     Analyzes execution flow of code submissions
 17 |     """
 18 |     
 19 |     def __init__(self):
 20 |         """Initialize the execution flow analyzer"""
 21 |         self.python_parser = PythonParser()
 22 |         self.cpp_parser = CppParser()
 23 |         self.java_parser = JavaParser()
 24 |     
 25 |     def analyze(self, code: str, language: ProgrammingLanguage) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 26 |         """
 27 |         Analyze execution flow of the given code
 28 |         
 29 |         Args:
 30 |             code: Source code to analyze
 31 |             language: Programming language of the code
 32 |             
 33 |         Returns:
 34 |             Dictionary containing execution flow analysis
 35 |         """
 36 |         logger.info(f"Analyzing execution flow for {language} code")
 37 |         
 38 |         try:
 39 |             # Parse the code based on language
 40 |             if language == ProgrammingLanguage.PYTHON:
 41 |                 parsed_data = self.python_parser.parse(code)
 42 |             elif language == ProgrammingLanguage.CPP:
 43 |                 parsed_data = self.cpp_parser.parse(code)
 44 |             elif language == ProgrammingLanguage.JAVA:
 45 |                 parsed_data = self.java_parser.parse(code)
 46 |             else:
 47 |                 return self._empty_flow()
 48 |             
 49 |             if not parsed_data.get('success', False):
 50 |                 logger.warning("Parsing failed, returning limited flow analysis")
 51 |                 return self._empty_flow()
 52 |             
 53 |             # Build execution flow from parsed data
 54 |             flow = self._build_execution_flow(parsed_data, language)
 55 |             
 56 |             logger.info("Execution flow analysis completed")
 57 |             return flow
 58 |             
 59 |         except Exception as e:
 60 |             logger.error(f"Error analyzing execution flow: {e}")
 61 |             return self._empty_flow()
 62 |     
 63 |     def _build_execution_flow(self, parsed_data: Dict[str, Any], 
 64 |                              language: ProgrammingLanguage) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 65 |         """
 66 |         Build execution flow structure from parsed data
 67 |         
 68 |         Args:
 69 |             parsed_data: Parsed code structure
 70 |             language: Programming language
 71 |             
 72 |         Returns:
 73 |             Execution flow dictionary
 74 |         """
 75 |         functions = parsed_data.get('functions', [])
 76 |         classes = parsed_data.get('classes', [])
 77 |         control_structures = parsed_data.get('control_structures', [])
 78 |         
 79 |         # Determine entry point
 80 |         entry_point = self._find_entry_point(functions, classes, language)
 81 |         
 82 |         # Build call graph
 83 |         call_graph = self._build_call_graph(functions)
 84 |         
 85 |         # Identify unreachable code
 86 |         unreachable = self._find_unreachable_code(functions, control_structures)
 87 |         
 88 |         return {
 89 |             'entry_point': entry_point,
 90 |             'functions': functions,
 91 |             'control_structures': control_structures,
 92 |             'call_graph': call_graph,
 93 |             'unreachable_code': unreachable
 94 |         }
 95 |     
 96 |     def _find_entry_point(self, functions: List[Dict[str, Any]],
 97 |                          classes: List[Dict[str, Any]],
 98 |                          language: ProgrammingLanguage) -> str | None:
 99 |         """
100 |         Find the entry point of the program
101 |         
102 |         Args:
103 |             functions: List of functions
104 |             classes: List of classes
105 |             language: Programming language
106 |             
107 |         Returns:
108 |             Entry point name or None
109 |         """
110 |         if language == ProgrammingLanguage.PYTHON:
111 |             # Look for if __name__ == "__main__" or top-level code
112 |             return "module_level"
113 |         
114 |         elif language == ProgrammingLanguage.CPP:
115 |             # Look for main function
116 |             for func in functions:
117 |                 if func.get('name') == 'main':
118 |                     return 'main'
119 |             return None
120 |         
121 |         elif language == ProgrammingLanguage.JAVA:
122 |             # Look for public static void main
123 |             for func in functions:
124 |                 if func.get('name') == 'main':
125 |                     modifiers = func.get('modifiers', [])
126 |                     if 'public' in modifiers and 'static' in modifiers:
127 |                         return 'main'
128 |             return None
129 |         
130 |         return None
131 |     
132 |     def _build_call_graph(self, functions: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
133 |         """
134 |         Build a call graph showing function relationships
135 |         
136 |         Args:
137 |             functions: List of functions
138 |             
139 |         Returns:
140 |             Dictionary mapping function names to called functions
141 |         """
142 |         call_graph = {}
143 |         
144 |         # Simplified call graph - in a real implementation, 
145 |         # we would analyze function bodies for calls
146 |         for func in functions:
147 |             func_name = func.get('name', 'unknown')
148 |             call_graph[func_name] = []
149 |         
150 |         return call_graph
151 |     
152 |     def _find_unreachable_code(self, functions: List[Dict[str, Any]], 
153 |                               control_structures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
154 |         """
155 |         Identify potentially unreachable code blocks
156 |         
157 |         Args:
158 |             functions: List of functions
159 |             control_structures: List of control structures
160 |             
161 |         Returns:
162 |             List of unreachable code blocks
163 |         """
164 |         unreachable = []
165 |         
166 |         # Simplified detection - would need more sophisticated analysis
167 |         # Look for code after return statements, infinite loops, etc.
168 |         
169 |         return unreachable
170 |     
171 |     def _empty_flow(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
172 |         """Return an empty execution flow structure"""
173 |         return {
174 |             'entry_point': None,
175 |             'functions': [],
176 |             'control_structures': [],
177 |             'call_graph': {},
178 |             'unreachable_code': []
179 |         }

 54 |             return {

 60 |     def _check_syntax_errors(self, code: str, language: ProgrammingLanguage,
 61 |                             parsed_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:

 66 |             code: Source code
 67 |             language: Programming language
 68 |             parsed_data: Parsed code structure
 69 |             
 70 |         Returns:
 71 |             List of syntax errors

 73 |         # First check if parser already found syntax errors
 74 |         parser_errors = parsed_data.get('syntax_errors', [])
 75 |         if parser_errors:
 76 |             return [self._format_syntax_error(err) for err in parser_errors]
 77 |         
 78 |         # Run language-specific linters
 79 |         if language == ProgrammingLanguage.PYTHON:
 80 |             return self._check_python_syntax(code)
 81 |         elif language == ProgrammingLanguage.CPP:
 82 |             return self._check_cpp_syntax(code)
 83 |         elif language == ProgrammingLanguage.JAVA:
 84 |             return self._check_java_syntax(code)
 85 |         
 86 |         return []

 88 |     def _check_python_syntax(self, code: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
 89 |         """Check Python syntax using pylint"""
 90 |         errors = []
 91 |         
 92 |         try:
 93 |             # Write code to temporary file
 94 |             with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.py', delete=False) as f:
 95 |                 f.write(code)
 96 |                 temp_file = f.name
 97 |             
 98 |             try:
 99 |                 # Run pylint
100 |                 result = subprocess.run(
101 |                     ['pylint', '--errors-only', '--output-format=json', temp_file],
102 |                     capture_output=True,
103 |                     text=True,
104 |                     timeout=10
105 |                 )
106 |                 
107 |                 if result.stdout:
108 |                     import json
109 |                     pylint_errors = json.loads(result.stdout)
110 |                     for err in pylint_errors:
111 |                         if err.get('type') in ('error', 'fatal'):
112 |                             errors.append({
113 |                                 'line': err.get('line', 0),
114 |                                 'column': err.get('column', 0),
115 |                                 'message': err.get('message', ''),
116 |                                 'code_snippet': self._get_code_snippet(code, err.get('line', 0)),
117 |                                 'severity': 'error'
118 |                             })
119 |             finally:
120 |                 os.unlink(temp_file)
121 |                 
122 |         except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
123 |             logger.warning("Pylint timeout")
124 |         except FileNotFoundError:
125 |             logger.warning("Pylint not found, skipping syntax check")
126 |         except Exception as e:
127 |             logger.error(f"Error running pylint: {e}")
128 |         
129 |         return errors

  1 | """
  2 | Bug Explainer
  3 | Converts technical error messages into plain-language explanations
  4 | """
  5 | 
  6 | from typing import Dict, List, Any
  7 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
  8 | 
  9 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 10 | 
 11 | 
 12 | class BugExplainer:
 13 |     """
 14 |     Provides plain-language explanations for bugs and errors
 15 |     """
 16 |     
 17 |     def __init__(self):
 18 |         """Initialize the bug explainer"""
 19 |         self.error_templates = self._load_error_templates()
 20 |     
 21 |     def explain(self, syntax_errors: List[Dict[str, Any]], 
 22 |                logic_errors: List[Dict[str, Any]],
 23 |                root_causes: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
 24 |         """
 25 |         Generate plain-language explanations for errors
 26 |         
 27 |         Args:
 28 |             syntax_errors: List of syntax errors
 29 |             logic_errors: List of logic errors
 30 |             root_causes: List of root causes
 31 |             
 32 |         Returns:
 33 |             List of explanations
 34 |         """
 35 |         logger.info("Generating plain-language explanations")
 36 |         
 37 |         explanations = []
 38 |         
 39 |         # Explain syntax errors
 40 |         for error in syntax_errors:
 41 |             explanation = self._explain_syntax_error(error)
 42 |             if explanation:
 43 |                 explanations.append(explanation)
 44 |         
 45 |         # Explain logic errors
 46 |         for error in logic_errors:
 47 |             explanation = self._explain_logic_error(error)
 48 |             if explanation:
 49 |                 explanations.append(explanation)
 50 |         
 51 |         # Limit to top 5 most important explanations
 52 |         return explanations[:5]
 53 |     
 54 |     def _explain_syntax_error(self, error: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 55 |         """
 56 |         Explain a syntax error in plain language
 57 |         
 58 |         Args:
 59 |             error: Syntax error details
 60 |             
 61 |         Returns:
 62 |             Plain-language explanation
 63 |         """
 64 |         message = error.get('message', '').lower()
 65 |         
 66 |         # Match error patterns and provide explanations
 67 |         if 'invalid syntax' in message:
 68 |             return self._create_explanation(
 69 |                 error_type='SyntaxError',
 70 |                 plain_explanation='There is a syntax error in your code. This means Python cannot understand what you wrote.',
 71 |                 why_it_happens='Syntax errors occur when code does not follow the language rules, like missing colons, parentheses, or quotes.',
 72 |                 how_to_fix='Check line {} for missing punctuation, incorrect indentation, or typos.'.format(error.get('line', 0)),
 73 |                 code_example=self._suggest_fix_for_syntax(error)
 74 |             )
 75 |         
 76 |         elif 'unexpected eof' in message or 'eof' in message:
 77 |             return self._create_explanation(
 78 |                 error_type='SyntaxError: Unexpected EOF',
 79 |                 plain_explanation='Python reached the end of your file but expected more code.',
 80 |                 why_it_happens='This usually means you have an unclosed bracket, parenthesis, or quote somewhere in your code.',
 81 |                 how_to_fix='Look for opening brackets, parentheses, or quotes that are not closed. Check all your function definitions and loops.',
 82 |                 code_example='Make sure every ( has a ), every [ has a ], and every { has a }'
 83 |             )
 84 |         
 85 |         elif 'indentation' in message:
 86 |             return self._create_explanation(
 87 |                 error_type='IndentationError',
 88 |                 plain_explanation='Your code indentation is incorrect.',
 89 |                 why_it_happens='Python uses indentation (spaces or tabs) to understand code structure. Mixing tabs and spaces or incorrect indentation causes errors.',
 90 |                 how_to_fix='Make sure all lines in the same block have the same indentation. Use either spaces or tabs consistently (4 spaces is recommended).',
 91 |                 code_example='if condition:\n    do_something()  # 4 spaces\n    do_another()    # 4 spaces'
 92 |             )
 93 |         
 94 |         elif 'name' in message and 'not defined' in message:
 95 |             return self._create_explanation(
 96 |                 error_type='NameError',
 97 |                 plain_explanation='You are trying to use a variable or function that does not exist.',
 98 |                 why_it_happens='This happens when you reference a variable before defining it, or when you have a typo in the name.',
 99 |                 how_to_fix='Check the spelling of the variable/function name. Make sure you define it before using it.',
100 |                 code_example='# Define before use:\nx = 10\nprint(x)  # Correct'
101 |             )
102 |         
103 |         elif 'missing' in message and 'parenthes' in message:
104 |             return self._create_explanation(
105 |                 error_type='SyntaxError: Missing Parenthesis',
106 |                 plain_explanation='You forgot to close a parenthesis.',
107 |                 why_it_happens='Every opening parenthesis ( must have a matching closing parenthesis ).',
108 |                 how_to_fix='Count your parentheses on line {} and make sure they match.'.format(error.get('line', 0)),
109 |                 code_example='result = calculate(a, b)  # Both ( and ) are present'
110 |             )
111 |         
112 |         # Default explanation for unknown syntax errors
113 |         return self._create_explanation(
114 |             error_type='Syntax Error',
115 |             plain_explanation='There is an error in your code syntax at line {}.'.format(error.get('line', 0)),
116 |             why_it_happens='The code does not follow the language rules.',
117 |             how_to_fix='Review line {} carefully for typos, missing punctuation, or incorrect structure.'.format(error.get('line', 0)),
118 |             code_example=error.get('code_snippet', '')
119 |         )
120 |     
121 |     def _explain_logic_error(self, error: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
122 |         """
123 |         Explain a logic error in plain language
124 |         
125 |         Args:
126 |             error: Logic error details
127 |             
128 |         Returns:
129 |             Plain-language explanation
130 |         """
131 |         error_type = error.get('type', '').lower()
132 |         
133 |         if 'infinite_loop' in error_type:
134 |             return self._create_explanation(
135 |                 error_type='Potential Infinite Loop',
136 |                 plain_explanation='Your loop might run forever without stopping.',
137 |                 why_it_happens='This happens when the loop condition never becomes false, so the loop keeps repeating.',
138 |                 how_to_fix='Make sure your loop has a condition that will eventually become false. Update the loop variable inside the loop.',
139 |                 code_example='# Good loop:\ni = 0\nwhile i < 10:\n    print(i)\n    i += 1  # This makes the loop end'
140 |             )
141 |         
142 |         elif 'null_pointer' in error_type or 'none' in error_type:
143 |             return self._create_explanation(
144 |                 error_type='Null/None Reference',
145 |                 plain_explanation='You are trying to use a variable that has no value (None/null).',
146 |                 why_it_happens='This happens when a variable is None/null and you try to access its properties or methods.',
147 |                 how_to_fix='Check if the variable is None before using it, or make sure it is properly initialized.',
148 |                 code_example='if my_var is not None:\n    my_var.do_something()'
149 |             )
150 |         
151 |         elif 'type_mismatch' in error_type:
152 |             return self._create_explanation(
153 |                 error_type='Type Mismatch',
154 |                 plain_explanation='You are trying to use a value of the wrong type.',
155 |                 why_it_happens='For example, trying to add a number to a string, or using a string where a number is expected.',
156 |                 how_to_fix='Make sure you are using the correct data types. Convert types if needed.',
157 |                 code_example='# Convert string to int:\nage = int("25")\nprint(age + 5)  # Now this works'
158 |             )
159 |         
160 |         # Default logic error explanation
161 |         return self._create_explanation(
162 |             error_type='Logic Error',
163 |             plain_explanation=error.get('message', 'There is a logic error in your code.'),
164 |             why_it_happens='The code runs but does not produce the expected result.',
165 |             how_to_fix=error.get('suggestion', 'Review the logic at line {}'.format(error.get('line', 0))),
166 |             code_example=''
167 |         )
168 |     
169 |     def _create_explanation(self, error_type: str, plain_explanation: str,
170 |                           why_it_happens: str, how_to_fix: str,
171 |                           code_example: str = '') -> Dict[str, Any]:
172 |         """
173 |         Create a structured explanation
174 |         
175 |         Args:
176 |             error_type: Type of error
177 |             plain_explanation: Simple explanation
178 |             why_it_happens: Why this error occurs
179 |             how_to_fix: How to fix it
180 |             code_example: Example code
181 |             
182 |         Returns:
183 |             Structured explanation dictionary
184 |         """
185 |         return {
186 |             'error_type': error_type,
187 |             'plain_explanation': plain_explanation,
188 |             'why_it_happens': why_it_happens,
189 |             'how_to_fix': how_to_fix,
190 |             'code_example': code_example if code_example else None
191 |         }
192 |     
193 |     def _suggest_fix_for_syntax(self, error: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
194 |         """Suggest a fix for a syntax error"""
195 |         # Simplified - would analyze the actual error in detail
196 |         return 'Check the syntax at line {}'.format(error.get('line', 0))
197 |     
198 |     def _load_error_templates(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:
199 |         """
200 |         Load error explanation templates
201 |         
202 |         Returns:
203 |             Dictionary of error templates
204 |         """
205 |         return {
206 |             'syntax_error': {
207 |                 'title': 'Syntax Error',
208 |                 'description': 'The code does not follow language rules'
209 |             },
210 |             'indentation_error': {
211 |                 'title': 'Indentation Error',
212 |                 'description': 'Incorrect spacing at the beginning of lines'
213 |             },
214 |             'name_error': {
215 |                 'title': 'Name Error',
216 |                 'description': 'Using a variable that does not exist'
217 |             },
218 |             'type_error': {
219 |                 'title': 'Type Error',
220 |                 'description': 'Using the wrong type of data'
221 |             },
222 |             'infinite_loop': {
223 |                 'title': 'Infinite Loop',
224 |                 'description': 'A loop that never ends'
225 |             }
226 |         }

  1 | """
  2 | FastAPI application for Efficiency Analyzer service
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
  6 | from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
  7 | from typing import Dict
  8 | import traceback
  9 | 
 10 | from .models.request import CodeAnalysisRequest
 11 | from .models.response import EfficiencyReport
 12 | from .services.complexity_calculator import ComplexityCalculator
 13 | from .services.pattern_detector import PatternDetector
 14 | from .services.optimizer import Optimizer
 15 | from .utils.logger import get_logger
 16 | 
 17 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 18 | 
 19 | # Initialize FastAPI app
 20 | app = FastAPI(
 21 |     title="Efficiency Analyzer Service",
 22 |     description="Analyzes code complexity and recommends optimizations",
 23 |     version="1.0.0"
 24 | )
 25 | 
 26 | # Add CORS middleware
 27 | app.add_middleware(
 28 |     CORSMiddleware,
 29 |     allow_origins=["*"],
 30 |     allow_credentials=True,
 31 |     allow_methods=["*"],
 32 |     allow_headers=["*"],
 33 | )
 34 | 
 35 | # Initialize services
 36 | complexity_calculator = ComplexityCalculator()
 37 | pattern_detector = PatternDetector()
 38 | optimizer = Optimizer()
 39 | 
 40 | 
 41 | @app.get("/health")
 42 | async def health_check() -> Dict[str, str]:
 43 |     """
 44 |     Health check endpoint
 45 |     
 46 |     Returns:
 47 |         Status information
 48 |     """
 49 |     return {
 50 |         "status": "healthy",
 51 |         "service": "efficiency-analyzer",
 52 |         "version": "1.0.0"
 53 |     }
 54 | 
 55 | 
 56 | @app.post("/api/v1/analyze", response_model=EfficiencyReport)
 57 | async def analyze_code(request: CodeAnalysisRequest) -> EfficiencyReport:
 58 |     """
 59 |     Analyze code for efficiency and provide optimization recommendations
 60 |     
 61 |     Args:
 62 |         request: Code analysis request containing code and language
 63 |         
 64 |     Returns:
 65 |         Efficiency analysis report with complexity and optimization strategies
 66 |         
 67 |     Raises:
 68 |         HTTPException: If analysis fails
 69 |     """
 70 |     try:
 71 |         logger.info(f"Analyzing {request.language} code ({len(request.code)} characters)")
 72 |         
 73 |         # Calculate complexity
 74 |         (
 75 |             time_complexity,
 76 |             space_complexity,
 77 |             target_time,
 78 |             target_space
 79 |         ) = complexity_calculator.calculate_complexity(
 80 |             request.code,
 81 |             request.language.value
 82 |         )
 83 |         
 84 |         # Detect inefficient patterns
 85 |         patterns = pattern_detector.detect_patterns(
 86 |             request.code,
 87 |             request.language.value
 88 |         )
 89 |         
 90 |         # Get optimization strategies
 91 |         strategies = optimizer.recommend_strategies(
 92 |             time_complexity.notation,
 93 |             patterns
 94 |         )
 95 |         
 96 |         # Estimate improvement
 97 |         estimated_improvement = optimizer.estimate_improvement(
 98 |             time_complexity.notation,
 99 |             target_time
100 |         )
101 |         
102 |         # Calculate overall efficiency score (0-100)
103 |         overall_score = _calculate_efficiency_score(
104 |             time_complexity.notation,
105 |             len(patterns)
106 |         )
107 |         
108 |         # Build report
109 |         report = EfficiencyReport(
110 |             current_time_complexity=time_complexity,
111 |             current_space_complexity=space_complexity,
112 |             target_time_complexity=target_time,
113 |             target_space_complexity=target_space,
114 |             inefficient_patterns=patterns,
115 |             optimization_strategies=strategies,
116 |             estimated_improvement=estimated_improvement,
117 |             overall_score=overall_score
118 |         )
119 |         
120 |         logger.info(
121 |             f"Analysis complete: {time_complexity.notation} time, "
122 |             f"{space_complexity.notation} space, "
123 |             f"{len(patterns)} patterns, "
124 |             f"score: {overall_score}"
125 |         )
126 |         
127 |         return report
128 |         
129 |     except Exception as e:
130 |         logger.error(f"Error analyzing code: {str(e)}")
131 |         logger.error(traceback.format_exc())
132 |         raise HTTPException(
133 |             status_code=500,
134 |             detail=f"Failed to analyze code: {str(e)}"
135 |         )
136 | 
137 | 
138 | def _calculate_efficiency_score(complexity: str, pattern_count: int) -> int:
139 |     """
140 |     Calculate overall efficiency score (0-100)
141 |     
142 |     Args:
143 |         complexity: Time complexity notation
144 |         pattern_count: Number of inefficient patterns detected
145 |         
146 |     Returns:
147 |         Efficiency score (higher is better)
148 |     """
149 |     # Base score from complexity
150 |     complexity_scores = {
151 |         'O(1)': 100,
152 |         'O(log n)': 90,
153 |         'O(n)': 75,
154 |         'O(n log n)': 60,
155 |         'O(n²)': 35,
156 |         'O(n³)': 15,
157 |         'O(2^n)': 5
158 |     }
159 |     
160 |     base_score = complexity_scores.get(complexity, 50)
161 |     
162 |     # Deduct points for patterns (max 5 points per pattern)
163 |     pattern_penalty = min(pattern_count * 5, 30)
164 |     
165 |     final_score = max(0, base_score - pattern_penalty)
166 |     
167 |     return final_score
168 | 
169 |

171 | async def root() -> Dict[str, str]:
172 |     """
173 |     Root endpoint with service information
174 |

177 |     """
178 |     return {
179 |         "service": "Efficiency Analyzer",

181 |         "description": "Analyzes code complexity and recommends optimizations",
182 |         "endpoints": {
183 |             "health": "/health",
184 |             "analyze": "/api/v1/analyze"
185 |         }
186 |     }
187 |

 1 | """
 2 | Logging configuration for Efficiency Analyzer service
 3 | """
 4 | 
 5 | import logging
 6 | import sys
 7 | from typing import Optional
 8 | 
 9 | 
10 | def get_logger(name: Optional[str] = None) -> logging.Logger:
11 |     """
12 |     Get a configured logger instance
13 |     
14 |     Args:
15 |         name: Logger name (defaults to root logger)
16 |         
17 |     Returns:
18 |         Configured logger instance
19 |     """
20 |     logger = logging.getLogger(name or __name__)
21 |     
22 |     # Only configure if no handlers exist
23 |     if not logger.handlers:
24 |         logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
25 |         
26 |         # Console handler
27 |         handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
28 |         handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)
29 |         
30 |         # Formatter
31 |         formatter = logging.Formatter(
32 |             '%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s',
33 |             datefmt='%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'
34 |         )
35 |         handler.setFormatter(formatter)
36 |         
37 |         logger.addHandler(handler)
38 |     
39 |     return logger
40 |

  1 | """
  2 | AST utility functions for code analysis
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | import ast
  6 | from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Set, Tuple
  7 | from .logger import get_logger
  8 | 
  9 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 10 | 
 11 | 
 12 | def parse_python_code(code: str) -> Optional[ast.AST]:
 13 |     """
 14 |     Parse Python code into an AST
 15 |     
 16 |     Args:
 17 |         code: Python source code
 18 |         
 19 |     Returns:
 20 |         AST node or None if parsing fails
 21 |     """
 22 |     try:
 23 |         return ast.parse(code)
 24 |     except SyntaxError as e:
 25 |         logger.error(f"Syntax error parsing code: {e}")
 26 |         return None
 27 |     except Exception as e:
 28 |         logger.error(f"Error parsing code: {e}")
 29 |         return None
 30 | 
 31 | 
 32 | def get_function_nodes(tree: ast.AST) -> List[ast.FunctionDef]:
 33 |     """
 34 |     Extract all function definition nodes from AST
 35 |     
 36 |     Args:
 37 |         tree: AST to analyze
 38 |         
 39 |     Returns:
 40 |         List of function definition nodes
 41 |     """
 42 |     functions = []
 43 |     for node in ast.walk(tree):
 44 |         if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
 45 |             functions.append(node)
 46 |     return functions
 47 | 
 48 | 
 49 | def get_loop_nodes(node: ast.AST) -> List[ast.AST]:
 50 |     """
 51 |     Extract all loop nodes (For, While) from AST
 52 |     
 53 |     Args:
 54 |         node: AST node to analyze
 55 |         
 56 |     Returns:
 57 |         List of loop nodes
 58 |     """
 59 |     loops = []
 60 |     for child in ast.walk(node):
 61 |         if isinstance(child, (ast.For, ast.While)):
 62 |             loops.append(child)
 63 |     return loops
 64 | 
 65 | 
 66 | def get_recursive_calls(func_node: ast.FunctionDef) -> List[ast.Call]:
 67 |     """
 68 |     Find recursive calls within a function
 69 |     
 70 |     Args:
 71 |         func_node: Function definition node
 72 |         
 73 |     Returns:
 74 |         List of recursive call nodes
 75 |     """
 76 |     func_name = func_node.name
 77 |     recursive_calls = []
 78 |     
 79 |     for node in ast.walk(func_node):
 80 |         if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
 81 |             if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id == func_name:
 82 |                 recursive_calls.append(node)
 83 |     
 84 |     return recursive_calls
 85 | 
 86 | 
 87 | def count_nested_loops(node: ast.AST) -> int:
 88 |     """
 89 |     Count maximum nesting level of loops
 90 |     
 91 |     Args:
 92 |         node: AST node to analyze
 93 |         
 94 |     Returns:
 95 |         Maximum nesting depth
 96 |     """
 97 |     def _count_depth(n: ast.AST, current_depth: int = 0) -> int:
 98 |         max_depth = current_depth
 99 |         
100 |         for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(n):
101 |             if isinstance(child, (ast.For, ast.While)):
102 |                 depth = _count_depth(child, current_depth + 1)
103 |                 max_depth = max(max_depth, depth)
104 |             else:
105 |                 depth = _count_depth(child, current_depth)
106 |                 max_depth = max(max_depth, depth)
107 |         
108 |         return max_depth
109 |     
110 |     return _count_depth(node)
111 | 
112 | 
113 | def get_loop_variable(loop_node: ast.For) -> Optional[str]:
114 |     """
115 |     Get the loop variable name from a For loop
116 |     
117 |     Args:
118 |         loop_node: For loop node
119 |         
120 |     Returns:
121 |         Variable name or None
122 |     """
123 |     if isinstance(loop_node.target, ast.Name):
124 |         return loop_node.target.id
125 |     return None
126 | 
127 | 
128 | def get_loop_iterable(loop_node: ast.For) -> Optional[str]:
129 |     """
130 |     Get the iterable expression from a For loop
131 |     
132 |     Args:
133 |         loop_node: For loop node
134 |         
135 |     Returns:
136 |         Iterable name or None
137 |     """
138 |     if isinstance(loop_node.iter, ast.Name):
139 |         return loop_node.iter.id
140 |     elif isinstance(loop_node.iter, ast.Call):
141 |         if isinstance(loop_node.iter.func, ast.Name):
142 |             return loop_node.iter.func.id
143 |     return None
144 | 
145 | 
146 | def analyze_data_structures(tree: ast.AST) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
147 |     """
148 |     Analyze data structure usage in code
149 |     
150 |     Args:
151 |         tree: AST to analyze
152 |         
153 |     Returns:
154 |         Dictionary mapping data structure types to variable names
155 |     """
156 |     data_structures = {
157 |         'list': [],
158 |         'dict': [],
159 |         'set': [],
160 |         'tuple': []
161 |     }
162 |     
163 |     for node in ast.walk(tree):
164 |         if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
165 |             for target in node.targets:
166 |                 if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
167 |                     var_name = target.id
168 |                     
169 |                     # Check value type
170 |                     if isinstance(node.value, ast.List):
171 |                         data_structures['list'].append(var_name)
172 |                     elif isinstance(node.value, ast.Dict):
173 |                         data_structures['dict'].append(var_name)
174 |                     elif isinstance(node.value, ast.Set):
175 |                         data_structures['set'].append(var_name)
176 |                     elif isinstance(node.value, ast.Tuple):
177 |                         data_structures['tuple'].append(var_name)
178 |                     elif isinstance(node.value, ast.Call):
179 |                         if isinstance(node.value.func, ast.Name):
180 |                             func_name = node.value.func.id
181 |                             if func_name in ['list', 'dict', 'set', 'tuple']:
182 |                                 data_structures[func_name].append(var_name)
183 |     
184 |     return data_structures
185 | 
186 | 
187 | def get_function_calls(node: ast.AST) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
188 |     """
189 |     Get all function calls with their line numbers
190 |     
191 |     Args:
192 |         node: AST node to analyze
193 |         
194 |     Returns:
195 |         List of (function_name, line_number) tuples
196 |     """
197 |     calls = []
198 |     
199 |     for child in ast.walk(node):
200 |         if isinstance(child, ast.Call):
201 |             if isinstance(child.func, ast.Name):
202 |                 func_name = child.func.id
203 |                 line_no = getattr(child, 'lineno', 0)
204 |                 calls.append((func_name, line_no))
205 |             elif isinstance(child.func, ast.Attribute):
206 |                 method_name = child.func.attr
207 |                 line_no = getattr(child, 'lineno', 0)
208 |                 calls.append((method_name, line_no))
209 |     
210 |     return calls
211 | 
212 | 
213 | def has_memoization(func_node: ast.FunctionDef) -> bool:
214 |     """
215 |     Check if a function uses memoization
216 |     
217 |     Args:
218 |         func_node: Function definition node
219 |         
220 |     Returns:
221 |         True if memoization is detected
222 |     """
223 |     # Check for @lru_cache decorator
224 |     for decorator in func_node.decorator_list:
225 |         if isinstance(decorator, ast.Name) and decorator.id == 'lru_cache':
226 |             return True
227 |         if isinstance(decorator, ast.Call):
228 |             if isinstance(decorator.func, ast.Name) and decorator.func.id == 'lru_cache':
229 |                 return True
230 |     
231 |     # Check for manual memoization (cache/memo dict)
232 |     for node in ast.walk(func_node):
233 |         if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
234 |             for target in node.targets:
235 |                 if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
236 |                     if 'cache' in target.id.lower() or 'memo' in target.id.lower():
237 |                         return True
238 |     
239 |     return False
240 | 
241 | 
242 | def get_comprehensions(tree: ast.AST) -> List[ast.AST]:
243 |     """
244 |     Get all list/dict/set comprehensions
245 |     
246 |     Args:
247 |         tree: AST to analyze
248 |         
249 |     Returns:
250 |         List of comprehension nodes
251 |     """
252 |     comprehensions = []
253 |     
254 |     for node in ast.walk(tree):
255 |         if isinstance(node, (ast.ListComp, ast.DictComp, ast.SetComp, ast.GeneratorExp)):
256 |             comprehensions.append(node)
257 |     
258 |     return comprehensions
259 | 
260 | # Made with Bob
</content>

  1 | """
  2 | Time complexity analyzer
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | import ast
  6 | from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
  7 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
  8 | from ..utils.ast_helpers import (
  9 |     get_loop_nodes,
 10 |     get_recursive_calls,
 11 |     count_nested_loops,
 12 |     get_function_calls,
 13 |     has_memoization
 14 | )
 15 | 
 16 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 17 | 
 18 | 
 19 | class TimeComplexityAnalyzer:
 20 |     """Analyzes time complexity of code"""
 21 |     
 22 |     # Built-in function complexities
 23 |     BUILTIN_COMPLEXITIES = {
 24 |         'len': 'O(1)',
 25 |         'append': 'O(1)',
 26 |         'pop': 'O(1)',
 27 |         'insert': 'O(n)',
 28 |         'remove': 'O(n)',
 29 |         'index': 'O(n)',
 30 |         'count': 'O(n)',
 31 |         'sort': 'O(n log n)',
 32 |         'sorted': 'O(n log n)',
 33 |         'min': 'O(n)',
 34 |         'max': 'O(n)',
 35 |         'sum': 'O(n)',
 36 |         'reversed': 'O(n)',
 37 |         'enumerate': 'O(1)',
 38 |         'zip': 'O(1)',
 39 |         'map': 'O(1)',
 40 |         'filter': 'O(1)',
 41 |         'any': 'O(n)',
 42 |         'all': 'O(n)',
 43 |         'in': 'O(n)',  # for lists
 44 |     }
 45 |     
 46 |     def __init__(self):
 47 |         self.complexity_factors = []
 48 |     
 49 |     def analyze(self, tree: ast.AST) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
 50 |         """
 51 |         Analyze time complexity of code
 52 |         
 53 |         Args:
 54 |             tree: AST to analyze
 55 |             
 56 |         Returns:
 57 |             Tuple of (complexity_notation, factors_list)
 58 |         """
 59 |         self.complexity_factors = []
 60 |         
 61 |         # Analyze functions
 62 |         for node in ast.walk(tree):
 63 |             if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
 64 |                 self._analyze_function(node)
 65 |         
 66 |         # If no functions, analyze top-level code
 67 |         if not self.complexity_factors:
 68 |             self._analyze_node(tree)
 69 |         
 70 |         # Calculate overall complexity
 71 |         complexity = self._calculate_overall_complexity()
 72 |         
 73 |         return complexity, self.complexity_factors
 74 |     
 75 |     def _analyze_function(self, func_node: ast.FunctionDef) -> None:
 76 |         """Analyze a single function"""
 77 |         # Check for recursion
 78 |         recursive_calls = get_recursive_calls(func_node)
 79 |         if recursive_calls:
 80 |             self._analyze_recursion(func_node, recursive_calls)
 81 |         
 82 |         # Analyze loops
 83 |         self._analyze_loops(func_node)
 84 |         
 85 |         # Analyze function calls
 86 |         self._analyze_function_calls(func_node)
 87 |     
 88 |     def _analyze_node(self, node: ast.AST) -> None:
 89 |         """Analyze a general AST node"""
 90 |         # Analyze loops
 91 |         self._analyze_loops(node)
 92 |         
 93 |         # Analyze function calls
 94 |         self._analyze_function_calls(node)
 95 |     
 96 |     def _analyze_loops(self, node: ast.AST) -> None:
 97 |         """Analyze loop complexity"""
 98 |         loops = get_loop_nodes(node)
 99 |         
100 |         if not loops:
101 |             return
102 |         
103 |         # Count nesting depth
104 |         max_depth = count_nested_loops(node)
105 |         
106 |         if max_depth == 1:
107 |             self.complexity_factors.append("Single loop: O(n)")
108 |         elif max_depth == 2:
109 |             self.complexity_factors.append("Nested loops (2 levels): O(n²)")
110 |         elif max_depth == 3:
111 |             self.complexity_factors.append("Nested loops (3 levels): O(n³)")
112 |         elif max_depth > 3:
113 |             self.complexity_factors.append(f"Nested loops ({max_depth} levels): O(n^{max_depth})")
114 |         
115 |         # Analyze individual loops
116 |         for loop in loops:
117 |             self._analyze_single_loop(loop)
118 |     
119 |     def _analyze_single_loop(self, loop_node: ast.AST) -> None:
120 |         """Analyze a single loop"""
121 |         if isinstance(loop_node, ast.For):
122 |             # Check if it's a range loop
123 |             if isinstance(loop_node.iter, ast.Call):
124 |                 if isinstance(loop_node.iter.func, ast.Name):
125 |                     func_name = loop_node.iter.func.id
126 |                     if func_name == 'range':
127 |                         # Analyze range arguments
128 |                         args = loop_node.iter.args
129 |                         if len(args) == 1:
130 |                             self.complexity_factors.append("Loop iterates n times")
131 |                         elif len(args) >= 2:
132 |                             # Could be range(0, n) or range(start, end)
133 |                             self.complexity_factors.append("Loop with range iteration")
134 |     
135 |     def _analyze_recursion(self, func_node: ast.FunctionDef, recursive_calls: List[ast.Call]) -> None:
136 |         """Analyze recursive function complexity"""
137 |         # Check for memoization
138 |         if has_memoization(func_node):
139 |             self.complexity_factors.append("Recursive with memoization: O(n)")
140 |             return
141 |         
142 |         # Count recursive calls per invocation
143 |         num_calls = len(recursive_calls)
144 |         
145 |         if num_calls == 1:
146 |             # Linear recursion (e.g., factorial)
147 |             self.complexity_factors.append("Linear recursion: O(n)")
148 |         elif num_calls == 2:
149 |             # Binary recursion (e.g., fibonacci)
150 |             self.complexity_factors.append("Binary recursion without memoization: O(2^n)")
151 |         else:
152 |             # Multiple recursive calls
153 |             self.complexity_factors.append(f"Multiple recursive calls ({num_calls}): O({num_calls}^n)")
154 |     
155 |     def _analyze_function_calls(self, node: ast.AST) -> None:
156 |         """Analyze complexity of function calls"""
157 |         calls = get_function_calls(node)
158 |         
159 |         for func_name, _ in calls:
160 |             if func_name in self.BUILTIN_COMPLEXITIES:
161 |                 complexity = self.BUILTIN_COMPLEXITIES[func_name]
162 |                 if complexity != 'O(1)':
163 |                     self.complexity_factors.append(f"{func_name}() call: {complexity}")
164 |     
165 |     def _calculate_overall_complexity(self) -> str:
166 |         """Calculate overall time complexity from factors"""
167 |         if not self.complexity_factors:
168 |             return "O(1)"
169 |         
170 |         # Look for dominant complexity
171 |         complexity_order = {
172 |             'O(1)': 0,
173 |             'O(log n)': 1,
174 |             'O(n)': 2,
175 |             'O(n log n)': 3,
176 |             'O(n²)': 4,
177 |             'O(n³)': 5,
178 |             'O(2^n)': 6,
179 |         }
180 |         
181 |         max_complexity = 'O(1)'
182 |         max_order = 0
183 |         
184 |         for factor in self.complexity_factors:
185 |             # Extract complexity notation from factor
186 |             if 'O(n³)' in factor or '3 levels' in factor:
187 |                 if complexity_order.get('O(n³)', 5) > max_order:
188 |                     max_complexity = 'O(n³)'
189 |                     max_order = 5
190 |             elif 'O(n²)' in factor or '2 levels' in factor or 'Nested loops' in factor:
191 |                 if complexity_order.get('O(n²)', 4) > max_order:
192 |                     max_complexity = 'O(n²)'
193 |                     max_order = 4
194 |             elif 'O(2^n)' in factor or 'Binary recursion without memoization' in factor:
195 |                 if complexity_order.get('O(2^n)', 6) > max_order:
196 |                     max_complexity = 'O(2^n)'
197 |                     max_order = 6
198 |             elif 'O(n log n)' in factor:
199 |                 if complexity_order.get('O(n log n)', 3) > max_order:
200 |                     max_complexity = 'O(n log n)'
201 |                     max_order = 3
202 |             elif 'O(n)' in factor:
203 |                 if complexity_order.get('O(n)', 2) > max_order:
204 |                     max_complexity = 'O(n)'
205 |                     max_order = 2
206 |             elif 'O(log n)' in factor:
207 |                 if complexity_order.get('O(log n)', 1) > max_order:
208 |                     max_complexity = 'O(log n)'
209 |                     max_order = 1
210 |         
211 |         return max_complexity
212 |     
213 |     def get_target_complexity(self, current_complexity: str) -> str:
214 |         """
215 |         Determine achievable target complexity
216 |         
217 |         Args:
218 |             current_complexity: Current complexity notation
219 |             
220 |         Returns:
221 |             Target complexity notation
222 |         """
223 |         # Mapping of current to target complexities
224 |         targets = {
225 |             'O(2^n)': 'O(n)',  # With memoization
226 |             'O(n³)': 'O(n²)',  # Reduce nesting
227 |             'O(n²)': 'O(n)',   # Use hash maps or better algorithms
228 |             'O(n log n)': 'O(n)',  # If sorting can be avoided
229 |             'O(n)': 'O(log n)',  # With binary search on sorted data
230 |             'O(log n)': 'O(1)',  # With hash maps
231 |             'O(1)': 'O(1)'  # Already optimal
232 |         }
233 |         
234 |         return targets.get(current_complexity, current_complexity)
235 | 
236 | # Made with Bob
</content>

<content lines="1-130">
  1 | """
  2 | Space complexity analyzer
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | import ast
  6 | from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
  7 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
  8 | from ..utils.ast_helpers import (
  9 |     analyze_data_structures,
 10 |     get_recursive_calls,
 11 |     get_comprehensions
 12 | )
 13 | 
 14 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 15 | 
 16 | 
 17 | class SpaceComplexityAnalyzer:
 18 |     """Analyzes space complexity of code"""
 19 |     
 20 |     def __init__(self):
 21 |         self.complexity_factors = []
 22 |     
 23 |     def analyze(self, tree: ast.AST) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
 24 |         """
 25 |         Analyze space complexity of code
 26 |         
 27 |         Args:
 28 |             tree: AST to analyze
 29 |             
 30 |         Returns:
 31 |             Tuple of (complexity_notation, factors_list)
 32 |         """
 33 |         self.complexity_factors = []
 34 |         
 35 |         # Analyze data structures
 36 |         data_structures = analyze_data_structures(tree)
 37 |         self._analyze_data_structures(data_structures)
 38 |         
 39 |         # Analyze recursion (call stack)
 40 |         self._analyze_recursion(tree)
 41 |         
 42 |         # Analyze comprehensions
 43 |         self._analyze_comprehensions(tree)
 44 |         
 45 |         # Calculate overall complexity
 46 |         complexity = self._calculate_overall_complexity()
 47 |         
 48 |         return complexity, self.complexity_factors
 49 |     
 50 |     def _analyze_data_structures(self, data_structures: Dict[str, List[str]]) -> None:
 51 |         """Analyze space used by data structures"""
 52 |         total_structures = sum(len(vars) for vars in data_structures.values())
 53 |         
 54 |         if total_structures == 0:
 55 |             self.complexity_factors.append("No auxiliary data structures: O(1)")
 56 |             return
 57 |         
 58 |         # Lists, dicts, sets typically use O(n) space
 59 |         for ds_type, vars in data_structures.items():
 60 |             if vars:
 61 |                 if ds_type in ['list', 'dict', 'set']:
 62 |                     self.complexity_factors.append(
 63 |                         f"{ds_type.capitalize()} data structure(s): O(n) space"
 64 |                     )
 65 |     
 66 |     def _analyze_recursion(self, tree: ast.AST) -> None:
 67 |         """Analyze space used by recursion (call stack)"""
 68 |         for node in ast.walk(tree):
 69 |             if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
 70 |                 recursive_calls = get_recursive_calls(node)
 71 |                 if recursive_calls:
 72 |                     # Recursive functions use call stack space
 73 |                     self.complexity_factors.append(
 74 |                         "Recursive call stack: O(n) space"
 75 |                     )
 76 |                     break
 77 |     
 78 |     def _analyze_comprehensions(self, tree: ast.AST) -> None:
 79 |         """Analyze space used by comprehensions"""
 80 |         comprehensions = get_comprehensions(tree)
 81 |         
 82 |         for comp in comprehensions:
 83 |             if isinstance(comp, ast.ListComp):
 84 |                 self.complexity_factors.append(
 85 |                     "List comprehension creates new list: O(n) space"
 86 |                 )
 87 |             elif isinstance(comp, ast.DictComp):
 88 |                 self.complexity_factors.append(
 89 |                     "Dict comprehension creates new dict: O(n) space"
 90 |                 )
 91 |             elif isinstance(comp, ast.SetComp):
 92 |                 self.complexity_factors.append(
 93 |                     "Set comprehension creates new set: O(n) space"
 94 |                 )
 95 |             elif isinstance(comp, ast.GeneratorExp):
 96 |                 # Generators are space-efficient
 97 |                 self.complexity_factors.append(
 98 |                     "Generator expression: O(1) space (lazy evaluation)"
 99 |                 )
100 |     
101 |     def _calculate_overall_complexity(self) -> str:
102 |         """Calculate overall space complexity from factors"""
103 |         if not self.complexity_factors:
104 |             return "O(1)"
105 |         
106 |         # Check if any factor indicates O(n) space
107 |         for factor in self.complexity_factors:
108 |             if 'O(n)' in factor:
109 |                 return "O(n)"
110 |         
111 |         # Otherwise, it's constant space
112 |         return "O(1)"
113 |     
114 |     def get_target_complexity(self, current_complexity: str) -> str:
115 |         """
116 |         Determine achievable target space complexity
117 |         
118 |         Args:
119 |             current_complexity: Current complexity notation
120 |             
121 |         Returns:
122 |             Target complexity notation
123 |         """
124 |         # Space complexity is harder to optimize than time
125 |         # Usually O(n) space is acceptable
126 |         if current_complexity == "O(n)":
127 |             return "O(1)"  # If we can use in-place operations
128 |         return current_complexity
129 | 
130 | # Made with Bob
</content>

<content lines="1-195">
  1 | """
  2 | Inefficient pattern detector
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | import ast
  6 | from typing import List, Dict
  7 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
  8 | from ..utils.ast_helpers import (
  9 |     get_loop_nodes,
 10 |     count_nested_loops,
 11 |     get_recursive_calls,
 12 |     has_memoization,
 13 |     get_function_calls
 14 | )
 15 | from ..models.response import InefficientPattern
 16 | 
 17 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 18 | 
 19 | 
 20 | class PatternAnalyzer:
 21 |     """Detects common inefficient code patterns"""
 22 |     
 23 |     def __init__(self):
 24 |         self.patterns = []
 25 |     
 26 |     def analyze(self, tree: ast.AST) -> List[InefficientPattern]:
 27 |         """
 28 |         Detect inefficient patterns in code
 29 |         
 30 |         Args:
 31 |             tree: AST to analyze
 32 |             
 33 |         Returns:
 34 |             List of detected inefficient patterns
 35 |         """
 36 |         self.patterns = []
 37 |         
 38 |         # Detect nested loops
 39 |         self._detect_nested_loops(tree)
 40 |         
 41 |         # Detect redundant recursion
 42 |         self._detect_redundant_recursion(tree)
 43 |         
 44 |         # Detect linear search in loops
 45 |         self._detect_linear_search_in_loop(tree)
 46 |         
 47 |         # Detect repeated sorting
 48 |         self._detect_repeated_sorting(tree)
 49 |         
 50 |         # Detect string concatenation in loops
 51 |         self._detect_string_concatenation_in_loop(tree)
 52 |         
 53 |         # Detect list operations in loops
 54 |         self._detect_list_operations_in_loop(tree)
 55 |         
 56 |         return self.patterns
 57 |     
 58 |     def _detect_nested_loops(self, tree: ast.AST) -> None:
 59 |         """Detect nested loops pattern"""
 60 |         max_depth = count_nested_loops(tree)
 61 |         
 62 |         if max_depth >= 2:
 63 |             # Find the nested loop locations
 64 |             for node in ast.walk(tree):
 65 |                 if isinstance(node, (ast.For, ast.While)):
 66 |                     # Check if this loop contains another loop
 67 |                     inner_loops = []
 68 |                     for child in ast.walk(node):
 69 |                         if child != node and isinstance(child, (ast.For, ast.While)):
 70 |                             inner_loops.append(child)
 71 |                     
 72 |                     if inner_loops:
 73 |                         line_numbers = [getattr(node, 'lineno', 0)]
 74 |                         for inner in inner_loops[:1]:  # Just first inner loop
 75 |                             line_numbers.append(getattr(inner, 'lineno', 0))
 76 |                         
 77 |                         severity = 'high' if max_depth >= 3 else 'medium'
 78 |                         
 79 |                         self.patterns.append(InefficientPattern(
 80 |                             pattern_type='nested_loops',
 81 |                             severity=severity,
 82 |                             line_numbers=line_numbers,
 83 |                             description=f'Nested loops with {max_depth} levels of nesting',
 84 |                             impact=f'O(n^{max_depth}) time complexity - performance degrades exponentially'
 85 |                         ))
 86 |                         break  # Only report once
 87 |     
 88 |     def _detect_redundant_recursion(self, tree: ast.AST) -> None:
 89 |         """Detect recursion without memoization"""
 90 |         for node in ast.walk(tree):
 91 |             if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
 92 |                 recursive_calls = get_recursive_calls(node)
 93 |                 
 94 |                 if len(recursive_calls) >= 2 and not has_memoization(node):
 95 |                     line_numbers = [getattr(node, 'lineno', 0)]
 96 |                     
 97 |                     self.patterns.append(InefficientPattern(
 98 |                         pattern_type='redundant_recursion',
 99 |                         severity='high',
100 |                         line_numbers=line_numbers,
101 |                         description='Multiple recursive calls without memoization',
102 |                         impact='Exponential time complexity O(2^n) - redundant calculations'
103 |                     ))
104 |     
105 |     def _detect_linear_search_in_loop(self, tree: ast.AST) -> None:
106 |         """Detect linear search operations inside loops"""
107 |         loops = get_loop_nodes(tree)
108 |         
109 |         for loop in loops:
110 |             # Check for 'in' operator with lists
111 |             for node in ast.walk(loop):
112 |                 if isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
113 |                     for op in node.ops:
114 |                         if isinstance(op, (ast.In, ast.NotIn)):
115 |                             # Check if comparing against a list/array
116 |                             line_no = getattr(node, 'lineno', 0)
117 |                             
118 |                             self.patterns.append(InefficientPattern(
119 |                                 pattern_type='linear_search_in_loop',
120 |                                 severity='medium',
121 |                                 line_numbers=[line_no],
122 |                                 description='Linear search (in operator) inside a loop',
123 |                                 impact='O(n²) time complexity - use set or dict for O(1) lookups'
124 |                             ))
125 |                             break
126 |     
127 |     def _detect_repeated_sorting(self, tree: ast.AST) -> None:
128 |         """Detect multiple sorting operations"""
129 |         sort_calls = []
130 |         
131 |         for node in ast.walk(tree):
132 |             if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
133 |                 if isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute):
134 |                     if node.func.attr == 'sort':
135 |                         line_no = getattr(node, 'lineno', 0)
136 |                         sort_calls.append(line_no)
137 |                 elif isinstance(node.func, ast.Name):
138 |                     if node.func.id == 'sorted':
139 |                         line_no = getattr(node, 'lineno', 0)
140 |                         sort_calls.append(line_no)
141 |         
142 |         if len(sort_calls) > 1:
143 |             self.patterns.append(InefficientPattern(
144 |                 pattern_type='repeated_sorting',
145 |                 severity='medium',
146 |                 line_numbers=sort_calls,
147 |                 description='Multiple sorting operations detected',
148 |                 impact='O(n log n) per sort - consider sorting once and maintaining order'
149 |             ))
150 |     
151 |     def _detect_string_concatenation_in_loop(self, tree: ast.AST) -> None:
152 |         """Detect string concatenation inside loops"""
153 |         loops = get_loop_nodes(tree)
154 |         
155 |         for loop in loops:
156 |             for node in ast.walk(loop):
157 |                 # Check for += with strings
158 |                 if isinstance(node, ast.AugAssign):
159 |                     if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add):
160 |                         line_no = getattr(node, 'lineno', 0)
161 |                         
162 |                         self.patterns.append(InefficientPattern(
163 |                             pattern_type='string_concatenation_in_loop',
164 |                             severity='medium',
165 |                             line_numbers=[line_no],
166 |                             description='String concatenation inside a loop',
167 |                             impact='O(n²) due to string immutability - use list and join() instead'
168 |                         ))
169 |                         break
170 |     
171 |     def _detect_list_operations_in_loop(self, tree: ast.AST) -> None:
172 |         """Detect inefficient list operations in loops"""
173 |         loops = get_loop_nodes(tree)
174 |         
175 |         for loop in loops:
176 |             for node in ast.walk(loop):
177 |                 if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
178 |                     if isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute):
179 |                         method = node.func.attr
180 |

182 |                         if method in ['insert', 'pop']:
183 |                             if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant):
184 |                                 if node.args[0].value == 0:
185 |                                     line_no = getattr(node, 'lineno', 0)
186 |                                     
187 |                                     self.patterns.append(InefficientPattern(
188 |                                         pattern_type='inefficient_list_operation',
189 |                                         severity='medium',
190 |                                         line_numbers=[line_no],
191 |                                         description=f'List.{method}(0) inside a loop',
192 |                                         impact='O(n) per operation - use deque for O(1) operations at both ends'
193 |                                     ))
