 16 | class ComplexityCalculator:
 17 |     """Calculates time and space complexity of code"""
 18 |     
 19 |     def __init__(self):
 20 |         self.time_analyzer = TimeComplexityAnalyzer()
 21 |         self.space_analyzer = SpaceComplexityAnalyzer()
 22 |     
 23 |     def calculate_complexity(
 24 |         self,
 25 |         code: str,
 26 |         language: str
 27 |     ) -> Tuple[ComplexityInfo, ComplexityInfo, str, str]:
 28 |         """
 29 |         Calculate time and space complexity
 30 |         
 31 |         Args:
 32 |             code: Source code to analyze
 33 |             language: Programming language
 34 |             
 35 |         Returns:
 36 |             Tuple of (time_complexity_info, space_complexity_info, 
 37 |                      target_time_complexity, target_space_complexity)
 38 |         """
 39 |         if language != "python":
 40 |             # For now, only Python is fully supported
 41 |             logger.warning(f"Language {language} not fully supported, using basic analysis")
 42 |             return self._basic_complexity_analysis()
 43 |         
 44 |         # Parse code
 45 |         tree = parse_python_code(code)
 46 |         if tree is None:
 47 |             logger.error("Failed to parse code")
 48 |             return self._basic_complexity_analysis()
 49 |         
 50 |         # Analyze time complexity
 51 |         time_notation, time_factors = self.time_analyzer.analyze(tree)
 52 |         time_complexity = ComplexityInfo(
 53 |             notation=time_notation,
 54 |             explanation=self._generate_time_explanation(time_notation, time_factors),
 55 |             factors=time_factors
 56 |         )
 57 |         
 58 |         # Analyze space complexity
 59 |         space_notation, space_factors = self.space_analyzer.analyze(tree)
 60 |         space_complexity = ComplexityInfo(
 61 |             notation=space_notation,
 62 |             explanation=self._generate_space_explanation(space_notation, space_factors),
 63 |             factors=space_factors
 64 |         )
 65 |         
 66 |         # Determine target complexities
 67 |         target_time = self.time_analyzer.get_target_complexity(time_notation)
 68 |         target_space = self.space_analyzer.get_target_complexity(space_notation)
 69 |         
 70 |         return time_complexity, space_complexity, target_time, target_space
 71 |     
 72 |     def _generate_time_explanation(self, notation: str, factors: List[str]) -> str:
 73 |         """Generate human-readable explanation of time complexity"""
 74 |         explanations = {
 75 |             'O(1)': 'Constant time - executes in fixed time regardless of input size',
 76 |             'O(log n)': 'Logarithmic time - typically from binary search or divide-and-conquer',
 77 |             'O(n)': 'Linear time - processes each element once',
 78 |             'O(n log n)': 'Linearithmic time - typical of efficient sorting algorithms',
 79 |             'O(n²)': 'Quadratic time - nested iterations over the data',
 80 |             'O(n³)': 'Cubic time - triple nested iterations',
 81 |             'O(2^n)': 'Exponential time - typically from unoptimized recursion'
 82 |         }
 83 |         
 84 |         base_explanation = explanations.get(notation, f'Time complexity is {notation}')
 85 |         
 86 |         if factors:
 87 |             return f"{base_explanation}. Contributing factors: {', '.join(factors[:3])}"
 88 |         
 89 |         return base_explanation
 90 |     
 91 |     def _generate_space_explanation(self, notation: str, factors: List[str]) -> str:
 92 |         """Generate human-readable explanation of space complexity"""
 93 |         explanations = {
 94 |             'O(1)': 'Constant space - uses fixed amount of memory',
 95 |             'O(n)': 'Linear space - memory usage grows with input size'
 96 |         }
 97 |         
 98 |         base_explanation = explanations.get(notation, f'Space complexity is {notation}')
 99 |         
100 |         if factors:
101 |             return f"{base_explanation}. Contributing factors: {', '.join(factors[:3])}"
102 |         
103 |         return base_explanation
104 |     
105 |     def _basic_complexity_analysis(self) -> Tuple[ComplexityInfo, ComplexityInfo, str, str]:
106 |         """Return basic complexity analysis when parsing fails"""
107 |         time_complexity = ComplexityInfo(
108 |             notation='O(n)',
109 |             explanation='Unable to perform detailed analysis',
110 |             factors=['Analysis limited due to parsing error']
111 |         )
112 |         
113 |         space_complexity = ComplexityInfo(
114 |             notation='O(1)',
115 |             explanation='Unable to perform detailed analysis',
116 |             factors=['Analysis limited due to parsing error']
117 |         )
118 |         
119 |         return time_complexity, space_complexity, 'O(n)', 'O(1)'

  2 | Optimization strategy recommender

  4 |

 12 | class Optimizer:
 13 |     """Recommends optimization strategies"""
 14 |     
 15 |     def __init__(self):
 16 |         self.strategy_templates = self._initialize_strategies()
 17 |     
 18 |     def recommend_strategies(
 19 |         self,
 20 |         current_time_complexity: str,
 21 |         patterns: List[InefficientPattern]
 22 |     ) -> List[OptimizationStrategy]:
 23 |         """
 24 |         Recommend optimization strategies based on complexity and patterns
 25 |         
 26 |         Args:
 27 |             current_time_complexity: Current time complexity notation
 28 |             patterns: List of detected inefficient patterns
 29 |             
 30 |         Returns:
 31 |             List of optimization strategies
 32 |         """
 33 |         strategies = []
 34 |         
 35 |         # Recommend based on patterns
 36 |         for pattern in patterns:
 37 |             strategy = self._get_strategy_for_pattern(pattern)
 38 |             if strategy and strategy not in strategies:
 39 |                 strategies.append(strategy)
 40 |         
 41 |         # Recommend based on complexity
 42 |         if current_time_complexity in ['O(n²)', 'O(n³)']:
 43 |             # Suggest general optimization for polynomial complexity
 44 |             general_strategy = self._get_general_optimization_strategy(current_time_complexity)
 45 |             if general_strategy and general_strategy not in strategies:
 46 |                 strategies.append(general_strategy)
 47 |         
 48 |         logger.info(f"Generated {len(strategies)} optimization strategies")
 49 |         
 50 |         return strategies
 51 |     
 52 |     def estimate_improvement(
 53 |         self,
 54 |         current_complexity: str,
 55 |         target_complexity: str
 56 |     ) -> Dict[str, str]:
 57 |         """
 58 |         Estimate performance improvement for different input sizes
 59 |         
 60 |         Args:
 61 |             current_complexity: Current complexity notation
 62 |             target_complexity: Target complexity notation
 63 |             
 64 |         Returns:
 65 |             Dictionary mapping input sizes to improvement estimates
 66 |         """
 67 |         improvements = {}
 68 |         
 69 |         # Define complexity growth rates
 70 |         complexity_values = {
 71 |             'O(1)': lambda n: 1,
 72 |             'O(log n)': lambda n: n.bit_length(),
 73 |             'O(n)': lambda n: n,
 74 |             'O(n log n)': lambda n: n * n.bit_length(),
 75 |             'O(n²)': lambda n: n * n,
 76 |             'O(n³)': lambda n: n * n * n,
 77 |             'O(2^n)': lambda n: 2 ** min(n, 20)  # Cap to prevent overflow
 78 |         }
 79 |         
 80 |         if current_complexity in complexity_values and target_complexity in complexity_values:
 81 |             current_func = complexity_values[current_complexity]
 82 |             target_func = complexity_values[target_complexity]
 83 |             
 84 |             for n in [100, 1000, 10000]:
 85 |                 current_ops = current_func(n)
 86 |                 target_ops = target_func(n)
 87 |                 
 88 |                 if target_ops > 0:
 89 |                     speedup = current_ops / target_ops
 90 |                     if speedup > 1:
 91 |                         improvements[f"n={n}"] = f"{speedup:.0f}x faster"
 92 |                     else:
 93 |                         improvements[f"n={n}"] = "Similar performance"
 94 |         
 95 |         return improvements
 96 |     
 97 |     def _initialize_strategies(self) -> Dict[str, OptimizationStrategy]:
 98 |         """Initialize optimization strategy templates"""
 99 |         return {
100 |             'nested_loops': OptimizationStrategy(
101 |                 technique='Hash Map / Set',
102 |                 description='Replace nested loops with hash-based lookups for O(1) access time',
103 |                 steps=[
104 |                     'Identify the inner loop operation (usually a search or comparison)',
105 |                     'Create a hash map or set to store elements for O(1) lookup',
106 |                     'Replace inner loop with hash map lookup',
107 |                     'Reduce time complexity from O(n²) to O(n)'
108 |                 ],
109 |                 complexity_improvement='O(n²) → O(n)',
110 |                 code_example='''# Before: O(n²)
111 | for i in range(len(arr)):
112 |     for j in range(len(arr)):
113 |         if arr[i] == arr[j]:
114 |             # ...
115 | 
116 | # After: O(n)
117 | seen = set()
118 | for item in arr:
119 |     if item in seen:
120 |         # ...
121 |     seen.add(item)'''
122 |             ),
123 |             'redundant_recursion': OptimizationStrategy(
124 |                 technique='Dynamic Programming (Memoization)',
125 |                 description='Cache recursive results to avoid redundant calculations',
126 |                 steps=[
127 |                     'Add a cache dictionary to store computed results',
128 |                     'Check cache before computing',
129 |                     'Store result in cache after computing',
130 |                     'Or use @lru_cache decorator in Python'
131 |                 ],
132 |                 complexity_improvement='O(2^n) → O(n)',
133 |                 code_example='''# Before: O(2^n)
134 | def fibonacci(n):
135 |     if n <= 1:
136 |         return n
137 |     return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)
138 | 
139 | # After: O(n)
140 | from functools import lru_cache
141 | 
142 | @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
143 | def fibonacci(n):
144 |     if n <= 1:
145 |         return n
146 |     return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)'''
147 |             ),
148 |             'linear_search_in_loop': OptimizationStrategy(
149 |                 technique='Set/Dict for O(1) Lookups',
150 |                 description='Convert list to set for constant-time membership testing',
151 |                 steps=[
152 |                     'Convert the search collection to a set before the loop',
153 |                     'Use set membership testing (O(1)) instead of list search (O(n))',
154 |                     'Maintain set if elements are added/removed'
155 |                 ],
156 |                 complexity_improvement='O(n²) → O(n)',
157 |                 code_example='''# Before: O(n²)
158 | for item in list1:
159 |     if item in list2:  # O(n) search
160 |         # ...
161 | 
162 | # After: O(n)
163 | set2 = set(list2)  # O(n) conversion
164 | for item in list1:
165 |     if item in set2:  # O(1) lookup
166 |         # ...'''
167 |             ),
168 |             'string_concatenation_in_loop': OptimizationStrategy(
169 |                 technique='List Join Pattern',
170 |                 description='Use list to collect strings, then join once at the end',
171 |                 steps=[
172 |                     'Create an empty list to collect string parts',
173 |                     'Append strings to the list in the loop',
174 |                     'Use str.join() to concatenate all parts at once',
175 |                     'Reduces from O(n²) to O(n)'
176 |                 ],
177 |                 complexity_improvement='O(n²) → O(n)',
178 |                 code_example='''# Before: O(n²)
179 | result = ""
180 | for item in items:
181 |     result += str(item)  # Creates new string each time
182 | 
183 | # After: O(n)
184 | parts = []
185 | for item in items:
186 |     parts.append(str(item))
187 | result = "".join(parts)'''
188 |             ),
189 |             'repeated_sorting': OptimizationStrategy(
190 |                 technique='Sort Once and Maintain Order',
191 |                 description='Sort data once and maintain sorted order, or use appropriate data structures',
192 |                 steps=[
193 |                     'Sort the data once at the beginning',
194 |                     'Use binary search for lookups (O(log n))',
195 |                     'Or use a heap/priority queue for maintaining sorted order',
196 |                     'Avoid re-sorting after each modification'
197 |                 ],
198 |                 complexity_improvement='O(n² log n) → O(n log n)',
199 |                 code_example='''# Before: Multiple sorts
200 | for item in items:
201 |     data.append(item)
202 |     data.sort()  # O(n log n) each time
203 | 
204 | # After: Sort once or use heap
205 | import heapq
206 | heap = []
207 | for item in items:
208 |     heapq.heappush(heap, item)  # O(log n) each time'''
209 |             ),
210 |             'inefficient_list_operation': OptimizationStrategy(
211 |                 technique='Use Deque for Efficient Operations',
212 |                 description='Use collections.deque for O(1) operations at both ends',
213 |                 steps=[

215 |                     'Replace list with deque',
216 |                     'Use appendleft() and popleft() for O(1) operations',
217 |                     'Convert back to list if needed'

223 | # list.insert(0, x) is O(n)

  1 | """
  2 | Request models for watsonx.ai Integration service
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | from enum import Enum
  6 | from typing import Optional, List, Dict, Any
  7 | from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, validator
  8 | 
  9 | 
 10 | class ProgrammingLanguage(str, Enum):
 11 |     """Supported programming languages"""
 12 |     PYTHON = "python"
 13 |     CPP = "cpp"
 14 |     JAVA = "java"
 15 | 
 16 | 
 17 | class OperationType(str, Enum):
 18 |     """Types of AI operations"""
 19 |     GENERATE = "generate"
 20 |     REFACTOR = "refactor"
 21 |     EXPLAIN = "explain"
 22 | 
 23 | 
 24 | class OptimizationTarget(str, Enum):
 25 |     """Optimization targets for code generation"""
 26 |     TIME_COMPLEXITY = "time_complexity"
 27 |     SPACE_COMPLEXITY = "space_complexity"
 28 |     READABILITY = "readability"
 29 |     BALANCED = "balanced"
 30 | 
 31 | 
 32 | class CodeGenerationRequest(BaseModel):
 33 |     """
 34 |     Request model for AI-powered code generation
 35 |     
 36 |     Attributes:
 37 |         problem_description: Natural language description of the problem
 38 |         language: Target programming language
 39 |         constraints: Optional constraints (e.g., "must use O(n) time")
 40 |         optimization_target: What to optimize for
 41 |         include_comments: Whether to include explanatory comments
 42 |         examples: Optional input/output examples
 43 |     """
 44 |     problem_description: str = Field(
 45 |         ...,
 46 |         min_length=10,
 47 |         max_length=5000,
 48 |         description="Natural language description of the problem to solve"
 49 |     )
 50 |     
 51 |     language: ProgrammingLanguage = Field(
 52 |         ...,
 53 |         description="Target programming language for generated code"
 54 |     )
 55 |     
 56 |     constraints: Optional[str] = Field(
 57 |         None,
 58 |         max_length=1000,
 59 |         description="Optional constraints (e.g., time/space complexity requirements)"
 60 |     )
 61 |     
 62 |     optimization_target: OptimizationTarget = Field(
 63 |         default=OptimizationTarget.BALANCED,
 64 |         description="What aspect to optimize for"
 65 |     )
 66 |     
 67 |     include_comments: bool = Field(
 68 |         default=True,
 69 |         description="Whether to include explanatory comments in generated code"
 70 |     )
 71 |     
 72 |     examples: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = Field(
 73 |         None,
 74 |         description="Optional input/output examples to guide generation"
 75 |     )
 76 |     
 77 |     webhook_url: Optional[str] = Field(
 78 |         None,
 79 |         description="Optional webhook URL for async result delivery"
 80 |     )
 81 |     
 82 |     @validator('problem_description')
 83 |     def validate_problem_description(cls, v):
 84 |         """Ensure problem description is meaningful"""
 85 |         if not v.strip():
 86 |             raise ValueError("Problem description cannot be empty")
 87 |         return v.strip()
 88 |     
 89 |     class Config:
 90 |         json_schema_extra = {
 91 |             "example": {
 92 |                 "problem_description": "Find all pairs in an array that sum to a target value",
 93 |                 "language": "python",
 94 |                 "constraints": "Must be O(n) time complexity",
 95 |                 "optimization_target": "time_complexity",
 96 |                 "include_comments": True,
 97 |                 "examples": [
 98 |                     {"input": "[2, 7, 11, 15], target=9", "output": "[(0, 1)]"}
 99 |                 ]
100 |             }
101 |         }
102 | 
103 | 
104 | class RefactoringRequest(BaseModel):
105 |     """
106 |     Request model for AI-powered code refactoring
107 |     
108 |     Attributes:
109 |         original_code: Code to be refactored
110 |         language: Programming language of the code
111 |         inefficient_patterns: List of detected inefficient patterns
112 |         target_complexity: Target time/space complexity
113 |         preserve_functionality: Whether to strictly preserve functionality
114 |         optimization_focus: What to focus on during refactoring
115 |     """
116 |     original_code: str = Field(
117 |         ...,
118 |         min_length=1,
119 |         max_length=50000,
120 |         description="Original code to be refactored"
121 |     )
122 |     
123 |     language: ProgrammingLanguage = Field(
124 |         ...,
125 |         description="Programming language of the code"
126 |     )
127 |     
128 |     inefficient_patterns: List[str] = Field(

 1 | """
 2 | Logging configuration for watsonx.ai Integration service
 3 | """
 4 | 
 5 | import logging
 6 | import sys
 7 | from typing import Optional
 8 | 
 9 | 
10 | def get_logger(name: Optional[str] = None) -> logging.Logger:
11 |     """
12 |     Get a configured logger instance
13 |     
14 |     Args:
15 |         name: Logger name (defaults to root logger)
16 |         
17 |     Returns:
18 |         Configured logger instance
19 |     """
20 |     logger = logging.getLogger(name or __name__)
21 |     
22 |     # Only configure if not already configured
23 |     if not logger.handlers:
24 |         # Set log level from environment or default to INFO
25 |         log_level = logging.INFO
26 |         
27 |         # Create console handler
28 |         handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
29 |         handler.setLevel(log_level)
30 |         
31 |         # Create formatter
32 |         formatter = logging.Formatter(
33 |             fmt='%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s',
34 |             datefmt='%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'
35 |         )
36 |         handler.setFormatter(formatter)
37 |         
38 |         # Add handler to logger
39 |         logger.addHandler(handler)
40 |         logger.setLevel(log_level)
41 |         
42 |         # Prevent propagation to avoid duplicate logs
43 |         logger.propagate = False
44 |     
45 |     return logger
46 | 
47 | 
48 | # Create default logger for the service
49 | service_logger = get_logger("watsonx-ai-integration")
50 | 
51 | # Made with Bob

  1 | """
  2 | Code generation service using watsonx.ai
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | import json
  6 | import time
  7 | from typing import Dict, Any
  8 | 
  9 | from ..models.request import CodeGenerationRequest
 10 | from ..models.response import GeneratedCode
 11 | from ..prompts.code_generation import build_generation_prompt
 12 | from ..utils.logger import get_logger
 13 | from .watsonx_client import WatsonxClient
 14 | 
 15 | logger = get_logger(__name__)
 16 | 
 17 | 
 18 | class CodeGeneratorService:
 19 |     """
 20 |     Service for AI-powered code generation
 21 |     Uses watsonx.ai to generate optimized code from problem descriptions
 22 |     """
 23 |     
 24 |     def __init__(self, watsonx_client: WatsonxClient):
 25 |         """
 26 |         Initialize code generator service
 27 |         
 28 |         Args:
 29 |             watsonx_client: Configured watsonx.ai client
 30 |         """
 31 |         self.client = watsonx_client
 32 |         logger.info("CodeGeneratorService initialized")
 33 |     
 34 |     async def generate_code(self, request: CodeGenerationRequest) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 35 |         """
 36 |         Generate optimized code from problem description
 37 |         
 38 |         Args:
 39 |             request: Code generation request
 40 |             
 41 |         Returns:
 42 |             Dictionary containing generated code and metadata
 43 |         """
 44 |         start_time = time.time()
 45 |         
 46 |         try:
 47 |             logger.info(f"Generating {request.language} code for problem")
 48 |             logger.debug(f"Problem: {request.problem_description[:100]}...")
 49 |             
 50 |             # Build prompt
 51 |             prompt = build_generation_prompt(
 52 |                 problem_description=request.problem_description,
 53 |                 language=request.language.value,
 54 |                 constraints=request.constraints,
 55 |                 optimization_target=request.optimization_target.value,
 56 |                 examples=request.examples
 57 |             )
 58 |             
 59 |             # Determine model and parameters based on complexity
 60 |             model_id = self._select_model(request)
 61 |             temperature = self._select_temperature(request.optimization_target.value)
 62 |             
 63 |             logger.debug(f"Using model: {model_id}, temperature: {temperature}")
 64 |             
 65 |             # Generate code using watsonx.ai
 66 |             response = await self.client.generate(
 67 |                 prompt=prompt,
 68 |                 model_id=model_id,
 69 |                 max_tokens=2048,
 70 |                 temperature=temperature,
 71 |                 top_p=0.95
 72 |             )
 73 |             
 74 |             # Parse response
 75 |             generated_code = self._parse_generation_response(response, request)
 76 |             
 77 |             processing_time = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000
 78 |             logger.info(f"Code generation completed in {processing_time:.2f}ms")
 79 |             
 80 |             return {
 81 |                 "success": True,
 82 |                 "generated_code": generated_code,
 83 |                 "processing_time_ms": processing_time,
 84 |                 "model_used": model_id,
 85 |                 "confidence_score": self._calculate_confidence(generated_code)
 86 |             }
 87 |             
 88 |         except Exception as e:
 89 |             logger.error(f"Code generation failed: {e}", exc_info=True)
 90 |             processing_time = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000
 91 |             
 92 |             return {
 93 |                 "success": False,
 94 |                 "error": str(e),
 95 |                 "processing_time_ms": processing_time
 96 |             }
 97 |     
 98 |     def _select_model(self, request: CodeGenerationRequest) -> str:
 99 |         """
100 |         Select appropriate model based on request complexity
101 |         
102 |         Args:
103 |             request: Code generation request
104 |             
105 |         Returns:
106 |             Model ID to use
107 |         """
108 |         # Use primary model for complex tasks, fast model for simple ones
109 |         problem_length = len(request.problem_description)
110 |         has_constraints = request.constraints is not None
111 |         has_examples = request.examples is not None and len(request.examples) > 0
112 |         
113 |         # Complex task indicators
114 |         if problem_length > 500 or has_constraints or has_examples:
115 |             return self.client.primary_model
116 |         else:
117 |             return self.client.fast_model
118 |     
119 |     def _select_temperature(self, optimization_target: str) -> float:
120 |         """
121 |         Select temperature based on optimization target
122 |         
123 |         Args:
124 |             optimization_target: What to optimize for
125 |             
126 |         Returns:
127 |             Temperature value (0-1)
128 |         """
129 |         # Lower temperature for time/space optimization (more deterministic)
130 |         # Higher temperature for readability (more creative)
131 |         temperature_map = {
132 |             "time_complexity": 0.3,
133 |             "space_complexity": 0.3,
134 |             "balanced": 0.5,
135 |             "readability": 0.7
136 |         }
137 |         return temperature_map.get(optimization_target, 0.5)
138 |     
139 |     def _parse_generation_response(
140 |         self,
141 |         response: Dict[str, Any],
142 |         request: CodeGenerationRequest
143 |     ) -> GeneratedCode:
144 |         """
145 |         Parse watsonx.ai response into GeneratedCode model
146 |         
147 |         Args:
148 |             response: Raw response from watsonx.ai
149 |             request: Original request
150 |             
151 |         Returns:
152 |             Parsed GeneratedCode object
153 |         """
154 |         try:
155 |             # Extract generated text
156 |             generated_text = response["results"][0]["generated_text"]
157 |             
158 |             # Try to parse as JSON
159 |             try:
160 |                 data = json.loads(generated_text)
161 |             except json.JSONDecodeError:
162 |                 # If not JSON, extract code from markdown or plain text
163 |                 data = self._extract_code_from_text(generated_text, request.language.value)
164 |             
165 |             # Create GeneratedCode object
166 |             return GeneratedCode(
167 |                 code=data.get("code", generated_text),
168 |                 language=request.language.value,
169 |                 algorithm_used=data.get("algorithm_used"),
170 |                 complexity_analysis={
171 |                     "time": data.get("time_complexity", "Not specified"),
172 |                     "space": data.get("space_complexity", "Not specified")
173 |                 },
174 |                 explanation=data.get("explanation"),
175 |                 test_cases=data.get("test_cases", [])
176 |             )
177 |             
178 |         except Exception as e:
179 |             logger.error(f"Failed to parse generation response: {e}")
180 |             # Return minimal valid response
181 |             return GeneratedCode(
182 |                 code="# Error parsing generated code\n# " + str(e),
183 |                 language=request.language.value,
184 |                 complexity_analysis={"time": "Unknown", "space": "Unknown"}
185 |             )
186 |     
187 |     def _extract_code_from_text(self, text: str, language: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
188 |         """
189 |         Extract code from plain text or markdown response
190 |         
191 |         Args:
192 |             text: Generated text
193 |             language: Programming language
194 |             
195 |         Returns:
196 |             Dictionary with extracted code and metadata
197 |         """
198 |         # Try to find code blocks
199 |         code_block_markers = [f"```{language}", "```python", "```java", "```cpp", "```"]
200 |         
201 |         code = text
202 |         for marker in code_block_markers:
203 |             if marker in text:
204 |                 parts = text.split(marker)
205 |                 if len(parts) >= 2:
206 |                     code = parts[1].split("```")[0].strip()
207 |                     break
208 |         
209 |         return {
210 |             "code": code,
211 |             "algorithm_used": "Not specified",
212 |             "time_complexity": "Not specified",
213 |             "space_complexity": "Not specified",
214 |             "explanation": "Generated code (parsing incomplete)"
215 |         }
216 |     
217 |     def _calculate_confidence(self, generated_code: GeneratedCode) -> float:
218 |         """
219 |         Calculate confidence score for generated code
220 |         
221 |         Args:
222 |             generated_code: Generated code object
223 |             
224 |         Returns:
225 |             Confidence score (0-1)
226 |         """
227 |         confidence = 0.5  # Base confidence
228 |         
229 |         # Increase confidence if we have good metadata
230 |         if generated_code.algorithm_used:
231 |             confidence += 0.15
232 |         
233 |         if generated_code.explanation:
234 |             confidence += 0.15
235 |         
236 |         if generated_code.complexity_analysis.get("time") != "Not specified":
237 |             confidence += 0.1
238 |         
239 |         if generated_code.test_cases:
240 |             confidence += 0.1
241 |         
242 |         # Check code quality indicators
243 |         code_lines = generated_code.code.split('\n')
244 |         if len(code_lines) > 3:  # Has substantial code
245 |             confidence += 0.05
246 |         
247 |         if any(keyword in generated_code.code for keyword in ['def ', 'class ', 'function ', 'public ']):
248 |             confidence += 0.05
249 |         
250 |         return min(confidence, 1.0)
251 |     
252 |     async def validate_generated_code(self, code: str, language: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
253 |         """
254 |         Validate generated code for syntax errors
255 |         
256 |         Args:
257 |             code: Generated code
258 |             language: Programming language
259 |             
260 |         Returns:
261 |             Validation results
262 |         """
263 |         # Basic syntax validation
264 |         # In production, this would use language-specific parsers
265 |         
266 |         validation_result = {
267 |             "is_valid": True,
268 |             "errors": [],
269 |             "warnings": []
270 |         }
271 |         
272 |         # Check for common issues
273 |         if not code.strip():
274 |             validation_result["is_valid"] = False
275 |             validation_result["errors"].append("Generated code is empty")
276 |         
277 |         # Language-specific checks
278 |         if language == "python":
279 |             # Check for basic Python syntax
280 |             try:
281 |                 compile(code, '<string>', 'exec')
282 |             except SyntaxError as e:
283 |                 validation_result["is_valid"] = False
284 |                 validation_result["errors"].append(f"Syntax error: {e}")
285 |         
286 |         return validation_result
287 |

 19 | class RefactoringService:
 20 |     """
 21 |     Service for AI-powered code refactoring
 22 |     Uses watsonx.ai to optimize code while preserving functionality
 23 |     """
 24 |     
 25 |     def __init__(self, watsonx_client: WatsonxClient):
 26 |         """
 27 |         Initialize refactoring service
 28 |         
 29 |         Args:
 30 |             watsonx_client: Configured watsonx.ai client
 31 |         """
 32 |         self.client = watsonx_client
 33 |         logger.info("RefactoringService initialized")
 34 |     
 35 |     async def refactor_code(self, request: RefactoringRequest) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 36 |         """
 37 |         Refactor and optimize code
 38 |         
 39 |         Args:
 40 |             request: Refactoring request
 41 |             
 42 |         Returns:
 43 |             Dictionary containing refactored code and metadata
 44 |         """
 45 |         start_time = time.time()
 46 |         
 47 |         try:
 48 |             logger.info(f"Refactoring {request.language} code")
 49 |             logger.debug(f"Original code length: {len(request.original_code)} chars")
 50 |             logger.debug(f"Inefficient patterns: {request.inefficient_patterns}")
 51 |             
 52 |             # Build prompt
 53 |             prompt = build_refactoring_prompt(
 54 |                 original_code=request.original_code,
 55 |                 language=request.language.value,
 56 |                 inefficient_patterns=request.inefficient_patterns,
 57 |                 target_complexity=request.target_complexity,
 58 |                 optimization_focus=request.optimization_focus.value
 59 |             )
 60 |             
 61 |             # Select model and temperature
 62 |             model_id = self.client.primary_model  # Always use primary for refactoring
 63 |             temperature = 0.2  # Low temperature for more deterministic refactoring
 64 |             
 65 |             logger.debug(f"Using model: {model_id}, temperature: {temperature}")
 66 |             
 67 |             # Generate refactored code using watsonx.ai
 68 |             response = await self.client.generate(
 69 |                 prompt=prompt,
 70 |                 model_id=model_id,
 71 |                 max_tokens=2048,
 72 |                 temperature=temperature,
 73 |                 top_p=0.9
 74 |             )
 75 |             
 76 |             # Parse response
 77 |             refactored_code = self._parse_refactoring_response(response, request)
 78 |             
 79 |             # Generate diff
 80 |             diff = self._generate_diff(
 81 |                 request.original_code,
 82 |                 refactored_code.refactored_code
 83 |             )
 84 |             refactored_code.diff = diff
 85 |             
 86 |             processing_time = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000
 87 |             logger.info(f"Code refactoring completed in {processing_time:.2f}ms")
 88 |             
 89 |             return {
 90 |                 "success": True,
 91 |                 "refactored_code": refactored_code,
 92 |                 "processing_time_ms": processing_time,
 93 |                 "model_used": model_id,
 94 |                 "confidence_score": self._calculate_confidence(refactored_code)
 95 |             }
 96 |             
 97 |         except Exception as e:
 98 |             logger.error(f"Code refactoring failed: {e}", exc_info=True)
 99 |             processing_time = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000
100 |             
101 |             return {
102 |                 "success": False,
103 |                 "error": str(e),
104 |                 "processing_time_ms": processing_time
105 |             }
106 |     
107 |     def _parse_refactoring_response(
108 |         self,
109 |         response: Dict[str, Any],
110 |         request: RefactoringRequest
111 |     ) -> RefactoredCode:
112 |         """
113 |         Parse watsonx.ai response into RefactoredCode model
114 |         
115 |         Args:
116 |             response: Raw response from watsonx.ai
117 |             request: Original request
118 |             
119 |         Returns:
120 |             Parsed RefactoredCode object
121 |         """
122 |         try:
123 |             # Extract generated text
124 |             generated_text = response["results"][0]["generated_text"]
125 |             
126 |             # Try to parse as JSON
127 |             try:
128 |                 data = json.loads(generated_text)
129 |             except json.JSONDecodeError:
130 |                 # If not JSON, extract code from text
131 |                 data = self._extract_refactored_code_from_text(
132 |                     generated_text,
133 |                     request.language.value
134 |                 )
135 |             
136 |             # Create RefactoredCode object
137 |             return RefactoredCode(
138 |                 original_code=request.original_code,
139 |                 refactored_code=data.get("refactored_code", generated_text),
140 |                 changes_made=data.get("changes_made", []),
141 |                 complexity_improvement={
142 |                     "before": data.get("complexity_before", {"time": "Unknown", "space": "Unknown"}),
143 |                     "after": data.get("complexity_after", {"time": "Unknown", "space": "Unknown"})
144 |                 },
145 |                 explanation=data.get("explanation", "Refactored code (parsing incomplete)"),
146 |                 preserved_functionality=request.preserve_functionality
147 |             )
148 |             
149 |         except Exception as e:
150 |             logger.error(f"Failed to parse refactoring response: {e}")
151 |             # Return minimal valid response
152 |             return RefactoredCode(
153 |                 original_code=request.original_code,
154 |                 refactored_code="# Error parsing refactored code\n# " + str(e),
155 |                 changes_made=[],
156 |                 complexity_improvement={
157 |                     "before": {"time": "Unknown", "space": "Unknown"},
158 |                     "after": {"time": "Unknown", "space": "Unknown"}
159 |                 },

161 |                 preserved_functionality=False

163 |     
164 |     def _extract_refactored_code_from_text(
165 |         self,
166 |         text: str,
167 |         language: str
168 |     ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
169 |         """
170 |         Extract refactored code from plain text response
171 |         
172 |         Args:
173 |             text: Generated text
174 |             language: Programming language
175 |             
176 |         Returns:
177 |             Dictionary with extracted code and metadata
178 |         """
179 |         # Try to find code blocks
180 |         code_block_markers = [f"```{language}", "```python", "```java", "```cpp", "```"]
181 |         
182 |         refactored_code = text
183 |         for marker in code_block_markers:
184 |             if marker in text:
185 |                 parts = text.split(marker)
186 |                 if len(parts) >= 2:
187 |                     refactored_code = parts[1].split("```")[0].strip()
188 |                     break
189 |         
190 |         return {
191 |             "refactored_code": refactored_code,
192 |             "changes_made": ["Extracted from text response"],
193 |             "complexity_before": {"time": "Not specified", "space": "Not specified"},
194 |             "complexity_after": {"time": "Not specified", "space": "Not specified"},
195 |             "explanation": "Refactored code (metadata incomplete)"
196 |         }
197 |     
198 |     def _generate_diff(self, original: str, refactored: str) -> str:
199 |         """
200 |         Generate unified diff between original and refactored code
201 |         
202 |         Args:
203 |             original: Original code
204 |             refactored: Refactored code
205 |             
206 |         Returns:
207 |             Unified diff string
208 |         """
209 |         original_lines = original.splitlines(keepends=True)
210 |         refactored_lines = refactored.splitlines(keepends=True)
211 |         
212 |         diff = difflib.unified_diff(
213 |             original_lines,
214 |             refactored_lines,
215 |             fromfile='original',
216 |             tofile='refactored',
217 |             lineterm=''
218 |         )
219 |         
220 |         return ''.join(diff)
221 |     
222 |     def _calculate_confidence(self, refactored_code: RefactoredCode) -> float:
223 |         """
224 |         Calculate confidence score for refactored code
225 |         
226 |         Args:
227 |             refactored_code: Refactored code object
228 |             
229 |         Returns:
230 |             Confidence score (0-1)
231 |         """
232 |         confidence = 0.5  # Base confidence
233 |         
234 |         # Increase confidence based on available metadata
235 |         if refactored_code.changes_made:
236 |             confidence += 0.15
237 |         
238 |         if refactored_code.explanation and len(refactored_code.explanation) > 50:
239 |             confidence += 0.15
240 |         
241 |         # Check if complexity improved
242 |         before = refactored_code.complexity_improvement.get("before", {})
243 |         after = refactored_code.complexity_improvement.get("after", {})
244 |         
245 |         if before.get("time") != "Unknown" and after.get("time") != "Unknown":
246 |             confidence += 0.1
247 |             # Check if actually improved
248 |             if self._is_complexity_improved(before.get("time"), after.get("time")):
249 |                 confidence += 0.1
250 |         
251 |         # Check code quality
252 |         if len(refactored_code.refactored_code.split('\n')) > 3:
253 |             confidence += 0.05
254 |         
255 |         return min(confidence, 1.0)
256 |     
257 |     def _is_complexity_improved(self, before: str, after: str) -> bool:
258 |         """
259 |         Check if complexity improved
260 |         
261 |         Args:
262 |             before: Original complexity
263 |             after: New complexity
264 |             
265 |         Returns:
266 |             True if improved
267 |         """
268 |         # Simple heuristic: check if O notation improved
269 |         complexity_order = {
270 |             "O(1)": 1,
271 |             "O(log n)": 2,
272 |             "O(n)": 3,
273 |             "O(n log n)": 4,
274 |             "O(n²)": 5,
275 |             "O(n^2)": 5,
276 |             "O(2^n)": 6,
277 |             "O(n!)": 7
278 |         }
279 |         
280 |         before_order = complexity_order.get(before, 999)
281 |         after_order = complexity_order.get(after, 999)
282 |         
283 |         return after_order < before_order
284 |     
285 |     async def analyze_refactoring_impact(
286 |         self,
287 |         original: str,
288 |         refactored: str
289 |     ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
290 |         """
291 |         Analyze the impact of refactoring
292 |         
293 |         Args:
294 |             original: Original code
295 |             refactored: Refactored code
296 |             
297 |         Returns:
298 |             Impact analysis
299 |         """
300 |         analysis = {
301 |             "lines_changed": 0,
302 |             "lines_added": 0,
303 |             "lines_removed": 0,
304 |             "similarity_score": 0.0
305 |         }
306 |         
307 |         # Calculate line changes
308 |         original_lines = original.splitlines()
309 |         refactored_lines = refactored.splitlines()
310 |         
311 |         analysis["lines_removed"] = len(original_lines) - len(refactored_lines)
312 |         analysis["lines_added"] = len(refactored_lines) - len(original_lines)
313 |         
314 |         # Calculate similarity
315 |         matcher = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, original, refactored)
316 |         analysis["similarity_score"] = matcher.ratio()
317 |         
318 |         # Count actual changes
319 |         diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(original_lines, refactored_lines))
320 |         analysis["lines_changed"] = len([line for line in diff if line.startswith('+') or line.startswith('-')])
321 |         
322 |         return analysis
323 |

 18 | class ExplainerService:
 19 |     """
 20 |     Service for AI-powered code explanation
 21 |     Uses watsonx.ai to generate educational explanations of code
 22 |     """
 23 |     
 24 |     def __init__(self, watsonx_client: WatsonxClient):
 25 |         """
 26 |         Initialize explainer service
 27 |         
 28 |         Args:
 29 |             watsonx_client: Configured watsonx.ai client
 30 |         """
 31 |         self.client = watsonx_client
 32 |         logger.info("ExplainerService initialized")
 33 |     
 34 |     async def explain_code(self, request: ExplanationRequest) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 35 |         """
 36 |         Generate comprehensive code explanation
 37 |         
 38 |         Args:
 39 |             request: Explanation request
 40 |             
 41 |         Returns:
 42 |             Dictionary containing explanation and metadata
 43 |         """
 44 |         start_time = time.time()
 45 |         
 46 |         try:
 47 |             logger.info(f"Explaining {request.language} code")
 48 |             logger.debug(f"Code length: {len(request.code)} chars")
 49 |             logger.debug(f"Explanation level: {request.explanation_level}")
 50 |             logger.debug(f"Focus areas: {request.focus_areas}")
 51 |             
 52 |             # Build prompt
 53 |             prompt = build_explanation_prompt(
 54 |                 code=request.code,
 55 |                 language=request.language.value,
 56 |                 explanation_level=request.explanation_level,
 57 |                 focus_areas=request.focus_areas,
 58 |                 bug_report=request.bug_report,
 59 |                 complexity_analysis=request.complexity_analysis,
 60 |                 include_analogies=request.include_analogies
 61 |             )
 62 |             
 63 |             # Select model based on explanation complexity
 64 |             model_id = self._select_model(request)
 65 |             temperature = self._select_temperature(request.explanation_level)
 66 |             
 67 |             logger.debug(f"Using model: {model_id}, temperature: {temperature}")
 68 |             
 69 |             # Generate explanation using watsonx.ai
 70 |             response = await self.client.generate(
 71 |                 prompt=prompt,
 72 |                 model_id=model_id,
 73 |                 max_tokens=1024,  # Explanations typically shorter than code
 74 |                 temperature=temperature,
 75 |                 top_p=0.95
 76 |             )
 77 |             
 78 |             # Parse response
 79 |             explanation = self._parse_explanation_response(response, request)
 80 |             
 81 |             processing_time = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000
 82 |             logger.info(f"Code explanation completed in {processing_time:.2f}ms")
 83 |             
 84 |             return {
 85 |                 "success": True,
 86 |                 "explanation": explanation,
 87 |                 "processing_time_ms": processing_time,
 88 |                 "model_used": model_id,
 89 |                 "confidence_score": self._calculate_confidence(explanation)
 90 |             }
 91 |             
 92 |         except Exception as e:
 93 |             logger.error(f"Code explanation failed: {e}", exc_info=True)
 94 |             processing_time = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000
 95 |             
 96 |             return {
 97 |                 "success": False,
 98 |                 "error": str(e),
 99 |                 "processing_time_ms": processing_time
100 |             }
101 |     
102 |     def _select_model(self, request: ExplanationRequest) -> str:
103 |         """
104 |         Select appropriate model based on explanation complexity
105 |         
106 |         Args:
107 |             request: Explanation request
108 |             
109 |         Returns:
110 |             Model ID to use
111 |         """
112 |         # Use fast model for simple explanations, primary for complex
113 |         has_context = request.bug_report is not None or request.complexity_analysis is not None
114 |         is_advanced = request.explanation_level == "advanced"
115 |         has_focus = request.focus_areas and len(request.focus_areas) > 0
116 |         
117 |         if has_context or is_advanced or has_focus:
118 |             return self.client.primary_model
119 |         else:
120 |             return self.client.fast_model
121 |     
122 |     def _select_temperature(self, explanation_level: str) -> float:
123 |         """
124 |         Select temperature based on explanation level
125 |         
126 |         Args:
127 |             explanation_level: Target audience level
128 |             
129 |         Returns:
130 |             Temperature value (0-1)
131 |         """
132 |         # Higher temperature for beginner (more creative/analogies)
133 |         # Lower temperature for advanced (more technical/precise)
134 |         temperature_map = {
135 |             "beginner": 0.8,
136 |             "intermediate": 0.6,
137 |             "advanced": 0.4
138 |         }
139 |         return temperature_map.get(explanation_level, 0.6)
140 |     
141 |     def _parse_explanation_response(
142 |         self,
143 |         response: Dict[str, Any],
144 |         request: ExplanationRequest
145 |     ) -> CodeExplanation:
146 |         """
147 |         Parse watsonx.ai response into CodeExplanation model
148 |         
149 |         Args:
150 |             response: Raw response from watsonx.ai
151 |             request: Original request
152 |             
153 |         Returns:
154 |             Parsed CodeExplanation object
155 |         """
156 |         try:
157 |             # Extract generated text
158 |             generated_text = response["results"][0]["generated_text"]
159 |             
160 |             # Try to parse as JSON
161 |             try:
162 |                 data = json.loads(generated_text)
163 |             except json.JSONDecodeError:
164 |                 # If not JSON, create structured explanation from text
165 |                 data = self._extract_explanation_from_text(generated_text)
166 |             
167 |             # Create CodeExplanation object
168 |             return CodeExplanation(
169 |                 summary=data.get("summary", "Code explanation generated"),
170 |                 detailed_explanation=data.get("detailed_explanation", generated_text),
171 |                 key_concepts=data.get("key_concepts", []),
172 |                 potential_issues=data.get("potential_issues", []),
173 |                 suggestions=data.get("suggestions", []),
174 |                 learning_resources=data.get("learning_resources", []),
175 |                 analogies=data.get("analogies", []) if request.include_analogies else []
176 |             )
177 |             
178 |         except Exception as e:
179 |             logger.error(f"Failed to parse explanation response: {e}")
180 |             # Return minimal valid response
181 |             return CodeExplanation(
182 |                 summary="Error generating explanation",
183 |                 detailed_explanation=f"An error occurred: {str(e)}",
184 |                 key_concepts=[],
185 |                 potential_issues=[],
186 |                 suggestions=[],
187 |                 learning_resources=[],
188 |                 analogies=[]
189 |             )
190 |     
191 |     def _extract_explanation_from_text(self, text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
192 |         """
193 |         Extract structured explanation from plain text
194 |         
195 |         Args:
196 |             text: Generated text
197 |             
198 |         Returns:
199 |             Dictionary with explanation components
200 |         """
201 |         # Simple extraction - split by common section headers
202 |         sections = {
203 |             "summary": "",
204 |             "detailed_explanation": text,
205 |             "key_concepts": [],
206 |             "potential_issues": [],
207 |             "suggestions": [],
208 |             "learning_resources": [],
209 |             "analogies": []
210 |         }
211 |         
212 |         # Try to extract summary (first paragraph)
213 |         paragraphs = text.split('\n\n')
214 |         if paragraphs:
215 |             sections["summary"] = paragraphs[0][:200]  # First 200 chars
216 |         
217 |         # Extract key concepts (look for bullet points or numbered lists)
218 |         lines = text.split('\n')
219 |         for line in lines:
220 |             if line.strip().startswith(('-', '*', '•')) or line.strip()[0:2].isdigit():
221 |                 concept = line.strip().lstrip('-*•0123456789. ')
222 |                 if concept and len(concept) > 5:
223 |                     sections["key_concepts"].append(concept)
224 |         
225 |         return sections
226 |     
227 |     def _calculate_confidence(self, explanation: CodeExplanation) -> float:
228 |         """
229 |         Calculate confidence score for explanation
230 |         
231 |         Args:
232 |             explanation: Code explanation object
233 |             
234 |         Returns:
235 |             Confidence score (0-1)
236 |         """
237 |         confidence = 0.5  # Base confidence
238 |         
239 |         # Increase confidence based on completeness
240 |         if explanation.summary and len(explanation.summary) > 20:
241 |             confidence += 0.1
242 |         
243 |         if explanation.detailed_explanation and len(explanation.detailed_explanation) > 100:
244 |             confidence += 0.15
245 |         
246 |         if explanation.key_concepts and len(explanation.key_concepts) > 0:
247 |             confidence += 0.1
248 |         
249 |         if explanation.suggestions and len(explanation.suggestions) > 0:
250 |             confidence += 0.1
251 |         
252 |         if explanation.analogies and len(explanation.analogies) > 0:
253 |             confidence += 0.05
254 |         
255 |         return min(confidence, 1.0)

313 |     def generate_learning_path(
314 |         self,
315 |         key_concepts: list,
316 |         current_level: str = "beginner"
317 |     ) -> list:
318 |         """
319 |         Generate a learning path based on identified concepts
320 |         
321 |         Args:
322 |             key_concepts: List of concepts from explanation
323 |             current_level: Current skill level
324 |             
325 |         Returns:
326 |             Ordered list of learning resources
327 |         """
328 |         # Map concepts to learning resources
329 |         concept_resources = {
330 |             "recursion": {
331 |                 "title": "Understanding Recursion",
332 |                 "topics": ["base case", "recursive case", "call stack"],
333 |                 "difficulty": "intermediate"
334 |             },
335 |             "dynamic programming": {
336 |                 "title": "Dynamic Programming Fundamentals",
337 |                 "topics": ["memoization", "tabulation", "optimal substructure"],
338 |                 "difficulty": "advanced"
339 |             },
340 |             "hash map": {
341 |                 "title": "Hash Tables and Maps",
342 |                 "topics": ["hashing", "collision resolution", "time complexity"],
343 |                 "difficulty": "beginner"
344 |             },
345 |             "two pointers": {
346 |                 "title": "Two Pointer Technique",
347 |                 "topics": ["array traversal", "optimization patterns"],
348 |                 "difficulty": "intermediate"
349 |             }
350 |         }
351 |         
352 |         learning_path = []
353 |         for concept in key_concepts:
354 |             concept_lower = concept.lower()
355 |             for key, resource in concept_resources.items():
356 |                 if key in concept_lower:
357 |                     learning_path.append(resource)
358 |                     break
359 |         
360 |         # Sort by difficulty based on current level
361 |         difficulty_order = {"beginner": 1, "intermediate": 2, "advanced": 3}
362 |         current_order = difficulty_order.get(current_level, 1)
363 |         
364 |         learning_path.sort(key=lambda x: abs(difficulty_order.get(x["difficulty"], 2) - current_order))
365 |         
366 |         return learning_path

101 |         
102 |         # Perform analysis
103 |         self.formatter.print_info("Step 1/4: Running debugging analysis...")
104 |         self.formatter.print_info("Step 2/4: Running efficiency analysis...")
105 |         self.formatter.print_info("Step 3/4: Generating refactored code...")
106 |         self.formatter.print_info("Step 4/4: Triggering automated actions...")
107 |         
108 |         results = self.client.complete_analysis(
109 |             code=code,
110 |             language=language,
111 |             include_refactoring=True,
112 |             include_automation=True
113 |         )
114 |         
115 |         # Display results
116 |         self.formatter.format_complete_analysis(results)
117 |     
118 |     def analyze_buggy_example(self):

159 |         
160 |         code = None
161 |         code_name = "Custom Code"

230 | {Fore.CYAN}{Style.BRIGHT}About Algorithmic Debugging & Efficiency Coach{Style.RESET_ALL}
231 | 
232 | {Fore.YELLOW}Overview:{Style.RESET_ALL}
233 | An intelligent code analysis system that diagnoses bugs and guides optimization
234 | from brute-force to production-ready solutions.
235 | 
236 | {Fore.YELLOW}Supported Languages:{Style.RESET_ALL}
237 |   • Python
238 |   • C++
239 |   • Java
240 | 
241 | {Fore.YELLOW}Core Features:{Style.RESET_ALL}
242 |   • {Fore.GREEN}Debugging Engine:{Style.RESET_ALL} Identifies bugs with execution flow analysis
243 |   • {Fore.GREEN}Efficiency Analyzer:{Style.RESET_ALL} Calculates time/space complexity
244 |   • {Fore.GREEN}watsonx.ai Integration:{Style.RESET_ALL} Generates refactored code
245 |   • {Fore.GREEN}watsonx Orchestrate:{Style.RESET_ALL} Automates documentation, tickets, and learning
246 | 
247 | {Fore.YELLOW}Architecture:{Style.RESET_ALL}
248 |   • Microservices-based design
249 |   • Containerized core services (Docker/Kubernetes)
250 |   • Serverless watsonx integrations
251 |   • Hybrid data layer (PostgreSQL + Redis + S3)
252 | 
253 | {Fore.YELLOW}Services:{Style.RESET_ALL}
254 |   • Debugging Engine (port 8001)
255 |   • Efficiency Analyzer (port 8002)
256 |   • watsonx.ai Integration (port 8003)
257 |   • watsonx Orchestrate Integration (port 8004)
258 | 
259 | {Fore.YELLOW}Target Users:{Style.RESET_ALL}
260 |   • Developers seeking code optimization
261 |   • Students learning algorithms
262 |   • Coding interview candidates
263 |   • Technical educators
264 | 
265 | {Fore.YELLOW}Technology Stack:{Style.RESET_ALL}
266 |   • Backend: Python (FastAPI), Node.js
267 |   • AI: IBM watsonx.ai, watsonx Orchestrate
268 |   • Database: PostgreSQL, Redis
269 |   • Storage: IBM Cloud Object Storage (S3)
270 |   • Deployment: Docker, Kubernetes, IBM Cloud Functions
271 | 
272 | For more information, see the project documentation.

274 |         print(about_text)
275 |     
276 |     def run(self):
277 |         """Run the CLI application."""
278 |         while True:
279 |             self.clear_screen()
280 |             self.print_banner()
281 |             self.print_menu()

283 |             choice = input(f"{Fore.GREEN}Enter your choice:{Style.RESET_ALL} ").strip()
284 |             
285 |             if choice == "1":
286 |                 self.analyze_buggy_example()
287 |                 input(f"\n{Fore.YELLOW}Press Enter to continue...{Style.RESET_ALL}")
288 |             elif choice == "2":

290 |                 input(f"\n{Fore.YELLOW}Press Enter to continue...{Style.RESET_ALL}")
291 |             elif choice == "3":

294 |             elif choice == "4":

297 |             elif choice == "5":

300 |             elif choice == "6":

302 |                 input(f"\n{Fore.YELLOW}Press Enter to continue...{Style.RESET_ALL}")
303 |             elif choice == "0":
304 |                 print(f"\n{Fore.CYAN}Thank you for using Algorithmic Debugging & Efficiency Coach!{Style.RESET_ALL}\n")
305 |                 sys.exit(0)

310 |

  1 | """API Client for communicating with all microservices."""
  2 | import requests
  3 | from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
  4 | import json
  5 | 
  6 | 
  7 | class APIClient:
  8 |     """Client to interact with all microservices."""
  9 |     
 10 |     def __init__(
 11 |         self,
 12 |         debugging_url: str = "http://localhost:8001",
 13 |         efficiency_url: str = "http://localhost:8002",
 14 |         watsonx_ai_url: str = "http://localhost:8003",
 15 |         watsonx_orchestrate_url: str = "http://localhost:8004"
 16 |     ):
 17 |         """Initialize API client with service URLs."""
 18 |         self.debugging_url = debugging_url
 19 |         self.efficiency_url = efficiency_url
 20 |         self.watsonx_ai_url = watsonx_ai_url
 21 |         self.watsonx_orchestrate_url = watsonx_orchestrate_url
 22 |         self.timeout = 30
 23 |     
 24 |     def analyze_debugging(self, code: str, language: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 25 |         """
 26 |         Send code to debugging engine for analysis.
 27 |         
 28 |         Args:
 29 |             code: Source code to analyze
 30 |             language: Programming language (python, cpp, java)
 31 |             
 32 |         Returns:
 33 |             Dictionary containing debugging analysis results
 34 |         """
 35 |         try:
 36 |             response = requests.post(
 37 |                 f"{self.debugging_url}/api/v1/analyze",
 38 |                 json={
 39 |                     "code": code,
 40 |                     "language": language
 41 |                 },
 42 |                 timeout=self.timeout
 43 |             )
 44 |             response.raise_for_status()
 45 |             return response.json()
 46 |         except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
 47 |             return {
 48 |                 "error": True,
 49 |                 "message": f"Debugging service error: {str(e)}",
 50 |                 "bugs": [],
 51 |                 "execution_flow": [],
 52 |                 "explanation": "Service unavailable"
 53 |             }
 54 |     
 55 |     def analyze_efficiency(self, code: str, language: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 56 |         """
 57 |         Send code to efficiency analyzer for complexity analysis.
 58 |         
 59 |         Args:
 60 |             code: Source code to analyze
 61 |             language: Programming language (python, cpp, java)
 62 |             
 63 |         Returns:
 64 |             Dictionary containing efficiency analysis results
 65 |         """
 66 |         try:
 67 |             response = requests.post(
 68 |                 f"{self.efficiency_url}/api/v1/analyze",
 69 |                 json={
 70 |                     "code": code,
 71 |                     "language": language
 72 |                 },
 73 |                 timeout=self.timeout
 74 |             )
 75 |             response.raise_for_status()
 76 |             return response.json()
 77 |         except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
 78 |             return {
 79 |                 "error": True,
 80 |                 "message": f"Efficiency service error: {str(e)}",
 81 |                 "time_complexity": {"current": "Unknown", "target": "Unknown"},
 82 |                 "space_complexity": {"current": "Unknown", "target": "Unknown"},
 83 |                 "patterns": [],
 84 |                 "optimization_steps": []
 85 |             }
 86 |     
 87 |     def generate_refactored_code(
 88 |         self,
 89 |         code: str,
 90 |         language: str,
 91 |         bugs: list,
 92 |         optimization_strategy: str
 93 |     ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 94 |         """
 95 |         Request watsonx.ai to generate refactored code.
 96 |         
 97 |         Args:
 98 |             code: Original source code
 99 |             language: Programming language
100 |             bugs: List of identified bugs
101 |             optimization_strategy: Recommended optimization approach
102 |             
103 |         Returns:
104 |             Dictionary containing refactored code and explanation
105 |         """
106 |         try:
107 |             response = requests.post(
108 |                 f"{self.watsonx_ai_url}/api/v1/refactor",
109 |                 json={
110 |                     "code": code,
111 |                     "language": language,
112 |                     "bugs": bugs,
113 |                     "optimization_strategy": optimization_strategy
114 |                 },
115 |                 timeout=self.timeout
116 |             )
117 |             response.raise_for_status()
118 |             return response.json()
119 |         except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
120 |             return {
121 |                 "error": True,
122 |                 "message": f"watsonx.ai service error: {str(e)}",
123 |                 "refactored_code": code,
124 |                 "explanation": "Service unavailable"
125 |             }
126 |     
127 |     def generate_explanation(
128 |         self,
129 |         code: str,
130 |         language: str,
131 |         bugs: list,
132 |         complexity: Dict[str, Any]
133 |     ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
134 |         """
135 |         Request watsonx.ai to generate plain-language explanation.
136 |         
137 |         Args:
138 |             code: Source code
139 |             language: Programming language
140 |             bugs: List of bugs
141 |             complexity: Complexity analysis results
142 |             
143 |         Returns:
144 |             Dictionary containing explanation
145 |         """
146 |         try:
147 |             response = requests.post(
148 |                 f"{self.watsonx_ai_url}/api/v1/explain",
149 |                 json={
150 |                     "code": code,
151 |                     "language": language,
152 |                     "bugs": bugs,
153 |                     "complexity": complexity
154 |                 },
155 |                 timeout=self.timeout
156 |             )
157 |             response.raise_for_status()
158 |             return response.json()
159 |         except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
160 |             return {
161 |                 "error": True,
162 |                 "message": f"watsonx.ai service error: {str(e)}",
163 |                 "explanation": "Service unavailable"
164 |             }
165 |     
166 |     def trigger_automated_actions(
167 |         self,
168 |         code: str,
169 |         language: str,
170 |         analysis_results: Dict[str, Any]
171 |     ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
172 |         """
173 |         Trigger watsonx Orchestrate workflows for automated actions.
174 |         
175 |         Args:
176 |             code: Source code
177 |             language: Programming language
178 |             analysis_results: Combined analysis results
179 |             
180 |         Returns:
181 |             Dictionary containing automated action results
182 |         """
183 |         try:
184 |             response = requests.post(
185 |                 f"{self.watsonx_orchestrate_url}/api/v1/automate",
186 |                 json={
187 |                     "code": code,
188 |                     "language": language,
189 |                     "analysis_results": analysis_results
190 |                 },
191 |                 timeout=self.timeout
192 |             )
193 |             response.raise_for_status()
194 |             return response.json()
195 |         except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
196 |             return {
197 |                 "error": True,
198 |                 "message": f"watsonx Orchestrate service error: {str(e)}",
199 |                 "documentation": {"status": "failed", "files": []},
200 |                 "tickets": {"status": "failed", "ticket_ids": []},
201 |                 "learning_path": {"status": "failed", "topics": []}
202 |             }
203 |     
204 |     def health_check(self) -> Dict[str, bool]:
205 |         """
206 |         Check health status of all services.
207 |         
208 |         Returns:
209 |             Dictionary with service names and their health status
210 |         """
211 |         services = {
212 |             "debugging_engine": self.debugging_url,
213 |             "efficiency_analyzer": self.efficiency_url,
214 |             "watsonx_ai": self.watsonx_ai_url,
215 |             "watsonx_orchestrate": self.watsonx_orchestrate_url
216 |         }
217 |         
218 |         health_status = {}
219 |         for service_name, url in services.items():
220 |             try:
221 |                 response = requests.get(f"{url}/health", timeout=5)
222 |                 health_status[service_name] = response.status_code == 200
223 |             except requests.exceptions.RequestException:
224 |                 health_status[service_name] = False
225 |         
226 |         return health_status
227 |     
228 |     def complete_analysis(
229 |         self,
230 |         code: str,
231 |         language: str,
232 |         include_refactoring: bool = True,
233 |         include_automation: bool = True
234 |     ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
235 |         """
236 |         Perform complete analysis including debugging, efficiency, and optional actions.
237 |         
238 |         Args:
239 |             code: Source code to analyze
240 |             language: Programming language
241 |             include_refactoring: Whether to generate refactored code
242 |             include_automation: Whether to trigger automated actions
243 |             
244 |         Returns:
245 |             Complete analysis results
246 |         """
247 |         results = {
248 |             "code": code,
249 |             "language": language,
250 |             "debugging": {},
251 |             "efficiency": {},
252 |             "refactoring": {},
253 |             "automation": {}
254 |         }
255 |         
256 |         # Step 1: Debugging analysis
257 |         results["debugging"] = self.analyze_debugging(code, language)
258 |         
259 |         # Step 2: Efficiency analysis
260 |         results["efficiency"] = self.analyze_efficiency(code, language)
261 |         
262 |         # Step 3: Optional refactoring
263 |         if include_refactoring and not results["debugging"].get("error"):
264 |             bugs = results["debugging"].get("bugs", [])
265 |             optimization_strategy = results["efficiency"].get("recommended_strategy", "General optimization")
266 |             results["refactoring"] = self.generate_refactored_code(
267 |                 code, language, bugs, optimization_strategy
268 |             )
269 |         
270 |         # Step 4: Optional automation
271 |         if include_automation:
272 |             results["automation"] = self.trigger_automated_actions(
273 |                 code, language, {
274 |                     "debugging": results["debugging"],
275 |                     "efficiency": results["efficiency"]
276 |                 }
277 |             )
278 |         
279 |         return results
280 | 
281 | # Made with Bob
